In photoreceptors, periciliary localization and human degeneration phenotypes connect the complex architecture to photoreceptor maintenance; the detailed quaternary interaction map was reconstructed with mouse protein fragments.

24-hydroxycholesterol 7-alpha-hydroxylase: as a microsomal cytochrome P450 monooxygenase, catalyzes the NADPH/O2-dependent 7-alpha-hydroxylation of (24S)-hydroxycholesterol, the committing oxysterol step of the alternative bile-acid synthesis pathway, in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane.
Binds heme as an essential cofactor for its P450 monooxygenase chemistry, coordinating the catalytic iron center that activates molecular oxygen.
Binds the heme iron ion via an axial protein ligand, forming the oxygen-activating catalytic center required for hydroxylation.

ALPK3 organizes the cardiomyocyte M-band protein network and supports formation and maintenance of a functional contractile apparatus. Human ALPK3 localization, partner association and loss-of-function studies connect it to myomesin and SQSTM1 positioning; the nuclear-envelope pool is documented in tagged immature human cardiomyocytes. An autonomous kinase or precisely defined bridging activity is not assigned while the catalytic conflict and the molecular organization of this network remain unresolved.

FGF-induced negative-feedback inhibitor acting at the receptor level: membrane IL17RD (hSef-a) associates with FGFR1 and FGFR2 (co-IP; ligand-independent; directness not established) and reduces FGF-induced FGFR1/FRS2 tyrosine phosphorylation and downstream Ras-RAF-MEK-ERK activation.

Spatial regulator of ERK signalling: binds activated MEK, retains the MEK-ERK complex at cytoplasmic/Golgi sites and blocks nuclear translocation of activated ERK, suppressing nuclear (Elk-1) but not cytoplasmic (RSK2) ERK outputs.

Dynein regulator that binds the cytoplasmic dynein intermediate and light chains and recruits LIS1 to autoinhibited dynein, promoting assembly of active dynein-dynactin-adaptor complexes before being displaced by dynactin; it acts at kinetochores (recruited by CENP-F; chromosome alignment and spindle orientation) and at the late-G2 nuclear envelope (NUP133-CENP-F platform; apical interkinetic nuclear migration and centrosome-nucleus coupling in neural progenitors).
Cargo adaptor for dynein: as a RAB9 effector, NDE1 tethers RAB9-GTP-positive late endosomes to dynein-dynactin-LIS1 for retrograde transport toward the trans-Golgi network.

Binds the cytoplasmic dynein-1 intermediate chain and recruits LIS1 to dynein, regulating dynein assembly with dynactin/adaptors and its force production; drives dynein-dependent nuclear translocation in migrating neurons and minus-end organelle transport.
At the mother centriole NDEL1 tethers dynein/dynactin and targets pericentriolar proteins, supporting microtubule anchoring at the centrosome.

Catalyzes metal-dependent endonucleolytic cleavage of exposed single-stranded regions in DNA hairpins and overhangs. In nuclear repair assemblies, Artemis opens coding-end hairpins for V(D)J recombination and processes complex DNA breaks before ligation during nonhomologous end joining. DNA-PKcs and the DNA/Ku context regulate access to these substrates.

Membrane recruitment of the Ras GAP neurofibromin: the SPRED2 EVH1 domain binds the NF1 GAP-related domain and the membrane-anchored SPR domain relocates it to the plasma membrane, promoting Ras-GTP hydrolysis and thereby dampening growth-factor-induced Ras-RAF-MEK-ERK signalling. SPRED2 is non-catalytic; the GAP catalysis is performed by neurofibromin.

TMEM63B forms a monomeric, small-conductance, high-threshold cation channel that opens in response to membrane tension and to hypo-osmotic swelling. It is permeable to Ca2+, Na+, K+ and Mg2+, and gates by the force-from-lipids mechanism rather than by ligand binding, so the osmolarity-sensing description (GO:1990760) and the mechanosensitive description refer to one activity. In alveolar type 2 cells this conductance converts lung inflation into the Ca2+ signal that drives lamellar body exocytosis.

TMEM63B translocates phospholipids bidirectionally between the two leaflets of the bilayer through a membrane-spanning hydrophilic groove, without ATP, when membrane curvature and thickness change or when tension is applied. Scrambling dissipates plasma membrane lipid asymmetry, exposing phosphatidylserine and redistributing phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin. The lipid pathway is resolved in open and closed cryo-EM structures and lies in the same groove as the ion pore, but is controlled by different bottleneck residues, so the scramblase and channel activities are separable; pathogenic variants around the hydrophobic gate make the scrambling constitutive without enhancing ion conduction. It remains to be shown that wild-type scrambling is deployed at physiological force in vivo.

All-trans-decaprenyl-diphosphate synthase (trans-prenyltransferase, EC 2.5.1.91): as a subunit of the PDSS1/PDSS2 heterotetramer (the activity is a property of the assembled complex), catalyzes the Mg(2+)-dependent sequential head-to-tail (trans) condensation of (2E,6E)-farnesyl diphosphate with seven isopentenyl diphosphate units to form all-trans-decaprenyl diphosphate (and, with six IPP units, the nonaprenyl diphosphate), the chain-length-determining step that builds the polyprenyl side chain of coenzyme Q10/Q9.

TREM2 is a plasma-membrane myeloid receptor that associates with TYROBP/DAP12 and transduces ligand binding into intracellular kinase, PLCG2, calcium, ERK, and activation programs in microglia and other myeloid cells.

TREM2 recognizes lipid-rich damage and uptake ligands, including aminophospholipids on apoptotic cells, lipoprotein/apolipoprotein particles, sulfatides, and amyloid-beta-lipoprotein complexes, enabling microglial phagocytosis, activation, migration, and lipid handling.

Stress-activated serine/threonine MAP kinase kinase kinase that phosphorylates MAP2Ks (MKK4/MKK7 and MKK3/MKK6) to activate the JNK and p38 (stress-activated) MAPK cascades, driving stress responses that can promote programmed cell death.

Proximal sensor of ribosome collisions in the ribotoxic stress response; isoform ZAKalpha directly binds the ribosome (inserting its C-terminus into the intersubunit space and contacting helix 14 of 18S rRNA), autophosphorylates upon collisions, and routes the signal to the JNK/p38 cell-death cascade or to GCN2-mediated integrated stress response.
Stress-activated MAPK signaling that triggers programmed cell death and, in response to UV-B/ribotoxic stress, the NLRP1 inflammasome and pyroptosis through direct NLRP1 phosphorylation.
Tight-junction scaffold that binds the YAP1 WW domains through its PPxY motifs, regulating YAP1 nucleocytoplasmic shuttling in Hippo signalling.
C-terminal PDZ-binding motif that engages the PDZ3 domain of MUPP1 and Patj at tight junctions.

AMP-preferring cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase that hydrolyzes AMP (and other ribo-/deoxyribonucleoside 5'-monophosphates) to the corresponding nucleoside plus inorganic phosphate, using a Mg2+ cofactor; the enzyme is allosterically activated by ADP.

In addition to ribonucleotide hydrolysis, cN-IA has measured 5'-deoxynucleotidase activity, hydrolyzing 2'-deoxyribonucleoside 5'-monophosphates such as dCMP; this contributes to broader nucleotide/nucleoside turnover and underlies its ability to dephosphorylate nucleoside-analog drugs.

Pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase (cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase 3A): Mg2+-dependent hydrolysis of pyrimidine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphates (UMP and CMP) to the corresponding nucleoside plus inorganic phosphate, degrading the pyrimidine nucleotides released by RNA turnover during erythroid maturation.
Requires magnesium as an active-site catalytic cofactor for its HAD-superfamily phosphoaspartate hydrolase mechanism.

Central scaffold of the super elongation complex. AFF4 uses separate, separately crystallised sites on its intrinsically disordered axis to hold cyclin T1 of P-TEFb and the C-terminal domain of ELL2 at the same time, and can bring those two elongation factors together with no other protein present. Assembled into the complex, it contributes to the stimulation of RNA polymerase II elongation and to the release of promoter-proximally paused polymerase; the bridging is AFF4's own activity, the stimulation is the complex's.

Transcription coregulator that couples locus-specific recruitment to elongation. The AFF4-containing complex is recruited to specific chromatin, including the target genes of MLL/KMT2A and its fusion oncoproteins, and AFF4 depletion lowers the expression of those targets. This is the family-level activity the AF4/FMR2 proteins share, and it is the level at which the phylogenetic annotations on this gene are correct. Recorded as a contribution rather than as AFF4's own activity, for the same reason as the elongation-factor activity above, namely that the coregulation is performed by the AFF4-containing complex being recruited to a locus, not by AFF4 in isolation, and the donor evidence behind the term is a gene-level genetic result in a fly with one family member rather than a measurement on an isolated protein. A first version of this review put it in molecular_function while putting the elongation activity in contributes_to, which was an unexplained asymmetry between two claims resting on the same kind of evidence; the concurrent AFF1 review (pull request 2348) independently placed the same term in contributes_to.

Self-association through the folded C-terminal homology domain. This is the only structured module of the protein, and the only AFF4 activity that requires no partner - two independent crystal structures of residues 899-1163 show a dimer, and single substitutions of Phe1014 or Tyr1096 impair it. The same surface also forms an AFF1-AFF4 heterodimer, and the domain carries a loop phosphorylated by CDK9.

Positive regulator of mesenchymal differentiation programmes. In human mesenchymal stem cells AFF4 is required for both adipogenic and osteogenic differentiation and its overexpression enhances both, with the adipogenic arm confirmed by an adipose-specific knockout mouse and the osteogenic arm by MSC-mediated bone formation in vivo. Both arms have a mapped mechanism. The adipogenic one runs through direct transcriptional activation of the autophagy genes ATG5 and ATG16L1, and the osteogenic one through BMP-pathway control of ID1 - AFF4 is enriched at the ID1 promoter by ChIP, its depletion lowers ID1 message and protein, and its depletion restricts BMP2-induced BRE-luciferase, SP7 and ALP responses. These are the best-evidenced endogenous processes the gene has. That alone would be an evidence argument rather than a core-ness one, so the core-ness claim is separate and narrower. These are the only contexts in which the scaffold's target SELECTIVITY has been measured rather than assumed. AFF4 and AFF1 occupy the same position in the same complex, yet depleting AFF1 has the opposite effect on osteogenesis, so these programmes are where the gene does something its paralogue does not - which is a property of the scaffold, not incidental pleiotropy in a ubiquitously expressed protein. Recorded rather than left as an asymmetry, the Sertoli-cell spermiogenesis requirement is deliberately NOT here, because it rests on a mouse knockout and is annotated in GOA on mouse Aff4 only, so this review does not annotate it on the human gene at all.

Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) adenylyltransferase: transfers an adenylyl group from ATP to NMN to form NAD+ with release of pyrophosphate (EC 2.7.7.1), the committed step of NAD+ biosynthesis via NMN.

Nicotinate mononucleotide (NaMN) adenylyltransferase: transfers an adenylyl group from ATP to NaMN to form nicotinate adenine dinucleotide (deamido-NAD+/NaAD) with release of pyrophosphate (EC 2.7.7.18); NMNAT1 uses the deamidated NaMN with comparable efficiency, linking the Preiss-Handler and de novo routes.

PGAP2 acts in the Golgi to carry out (or to be required for) the second step of GPI fatty-acid remodeling, reacylating the lyso-GPI intermediate with a saturated stearoyl chain after PGAP3 removes the sn-2 unsaturated fatty acid; this generates the mature, lipid-raft-associating GPI anchor needed for stable cell-surface expression of GPI-anchored proteins.
PGAP2 is required for GPI-anchor biosynthesis/maturation; loss of function reduces cell-surface expression of GPI-anchored proteins (e.g. DAF/CD55, CD59), and hypomorphic variants cause HPMRS3.

ALKBH1 catalyses the second, oxidative half of wobble-base maturation in mitochondrial tRNA-Met. Acting on the 5-methylcytidine that NSUN3 installs at position 34, it performs two successive Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent oxidations - first to 5-hydroxymethylcytidine, then to 5-formylcytidine (f5C34). f5C34 is what allows the single mitochondrial tRNA-Met to read AUA and AUU as methionine in addition to AUG under the non-universal mitochondrial genetic code, so the modification is required for normal mitochondrial translation and for assembly of functional respiratory complexes. ALKBH1 performs the analogous reaction on 2'-O-methylated cytidine 34 of cytoplasmic tRNA-Leu.

ALKBH1 oxidatively removes the methyl group from N1-methyladenosine in cytoplasmic and mitochondrial tRNAs. Lowering m1A levels reduces the usage of the affected tRNAs in protein synthesis and attenuates translation initiation, and the activity is responsive to glucose availability, making it a nutrient-linked input into translational output. The same reaction on mitochondrial tRNAs was detected independently as an increase in m1A in ALKBH1-knockout cells.

ALKBH1 binds a single catalytic Fe(II) ion at the conserved 2-His-1-carboxylate facial triad of its double-stranded beta-helix fold, together with 2-oxoglutarate as co-substrate. This cofactor centre generates the ferryl intermediate used by every oxidative reaction the protein performs, on tRNA and on nucleic acids generally; mutation of the predicted Fe(II)- and 2-oxoglutarate-binding residues abolishes activity.

Structural root component of the mother-centriole distal appendages (ciliary transition fibers). CEP83 is required to assemble the appendages by recruiting SCLT1 and CEP89 (and through SCLT1, FBF1 and CEP164), and thereby enables docking of the mother centriole to ciliary vesicles and the plasma membrane, TTBK2 recruitment, CP110 removal and initiation of primary cilium assembly.
Apical Ser/Thr protein kinase of the Myddosome that phosphorylates IRAK1, IRAK2 and Pellino proteins to propagate TLR and IL-1 receptor signals.

Death-domain scaffold that is recruited by MyD88 and recruits IRAK2/IRAK1, assembling the Myddosome; kinase-independent scaffolding also integrates MYD88 and TRIF signalling to TRAF6 in TLR4 signalling.
Transfers the second galactose onto the protein-linked Gal-Xyl acceptor in the medial Golgi, supplying the third sugar of the common proteoglycan GAG linker.

NAGS catalyzes the acetylation of L-glutamate by acetyl-CoA to produce N-acetyl-L-glutamate (NAG) and CoA (EC 2.3.1.1) in the mitochondrial matrix. NAG is the obligate allosteric activator of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 (CPS1), so NAGS provides the essential regulatory input that gates the urea cycle and hepatic ammonia detoxification.

COA6 reduces disulfides in copper-site assembly clients in the mitochondrial intermembrane space, enabling MT-CO2 CuA maturation and complex-IV biogenesis. Purified human protein reduces SCO1, SCO2 and COX2; cellular redox effects are demonstrated for SCO proteins with model-dependent substrate responses. Copper binding is experimentally supported, but autonomous copper delivery is not established.
Bind DNA and contribute to PBAF-dependent chromatin remodeling and promoter-selective transcriptional regulation. ATP hydrolysis is supplied by BRG1 rather than ARID2.
Support RAD51 recruitment and homologous-recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks. The precise contribution of BRG1-containing and BRG1-independent assemblies remains unresolved.

ARID1B binds DNA without apparent sequence preference and supplies assembly contacts to human SWI/SNF complexes, contributing to cooperative nucleosome engagement and ATP-driven chromatin remodeling. SMARCA2 or SMARCA4 provides the ATPase.

Human hOsa2/ARID1B supports transcriptional coactivation by steroid receptors as part of SWI/SNF, with an intact DNA-binding region required in the tested GR reporter context. Reporter conditions distinguish human ARID1B from rat GR and human ER/AR reagents.

Recognizes cis-regulatory DNA and regulates RNA polymerase II transcription, repressing targets such as LMO1/SHOX2 and enhancing KDM5C activation together with PHF8. This nuclear activity contributes to neuronal development and selected pancreatic and intestinal endocrine differentiation programs; direct downstream targets for every developmental context remain unresolved.
Binds microtubules, associates with kinesin-2 machinery, and supports ciliary axoneme formation and length control.
Restrains canonical Wnt signaling output in a context linked to epithelial ciliogenesis.

Molybdenum cofactor sulfurase: MOCOS catalyzes the PLP-dependent transfer of sulfur from L-cysteine to the molybdenum cofactor, converting Mo-molybdopterin to its terminal-sulfido (thio) form (EC 2.8.1.9). The N-terminal NifS-like domain performs L-cysteine desulfurase chemistry (L-cysteine to L-alanine plus an enzyme persulfide) and the C-terminal MOSC domain delivers the sulfur to the bound Moco. The sulfurated MoCo is specifically required to activate xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase and aldehyde oxidase.

Pyridoxal-5'-phosphate binding: MOCOS is a class-V PLP-dependent enzyme; PLP is covalently bound at Lys264 in the NifS-like domain and is the essential catalytic cofactor for the L-cysteine desulfurase step. Pathogenic variants that reduce PLP binding abolish the sulfur-mobilizing activity.

Supports assembly of the ELP1–ELP2–ELP3 subcomplex and contributes to Elongator-catalyzed formation of carboxymethyluridine at tRNA position 34. ELP3 performs the catalytic chemistry; ELP2 provides a structural contribution within the complex.

Transmembrane myosin VIIA-binding adaptor activity at adherens junctions. Vezatin, anchored in the junctional plasma membrane by its two transmembrane helices, binds the C-terminal FERM domain of myosin VIIA through its cytoplasmic C-terminal region and thereby bridges the cadherin-catenin adhesion complex (to which it is recruited via the E-cadherin cytoplasmic tail and the C-terminal region of alpha-catenin) to the actomyosin cytoskeleton, with an additional link to cortical actin through the open, actin-binding conformation of radixin. This tension-generating coupling is dispensable for junction formation but required for the maintenance and mechanical stability of already-formed junctions - loss of vezatin delocalizes E-cadherin and beta-catenin from the plasma membrane, disrupts intercellular adhesion, and renders cochlear hair cells acutely vulnerable to acoustic overstimulation.

Ankle-link complex component at the base of developing hair-cell stereocilia. Vezatin is conveyed to the stereocilia base by myosin VIIA, whose C-terminal FERM domain it binds, and there it is an integral membrane constituent of the transient ankle-link complex together with ADGRV1/VLGR1, usherin and whirlin, binding the usherin cytoplasmic region directly. Through this complex it participates in the cohesion and differentiation of the growing hair bundle and hence in inner-ear stereocilium organization and the sensory perception of sound; vezatin is lost from the stereocilia base in Vlgr1-null, Myo7a-null and whirlin-null mice, and its presence tracks the developmental appearance and disappearance of the ankle links.

N-terminal palmitoylation of the Hedgehog morphogens. HHAT transfers palmitate from palmitoyl-CoA onto the alpha-amino group of the N-terminal cysteine of autoprocessed Sonic, Desert and Indian Hedgehog, forming an amide bond, with Asp339 and His379 as the catalytic residues and a bound heme b required for activity. Catalysis happens inside the ER membrane: palmitoyl-CoA reaches the reaction chamber from the cytosolic leaflet and the Hedgehog peptide from the lumen, and the enzyme also promotes movement of palmitoyl-CoA to the luminal side. The reaction is the last covalent step of Hedgehog ligand maturation, after autocleavage and autocholesterylation, and the palmitate it installs is what the receptor Patched reads - which is why the modification is required for Hedgehog signalling at both ranges and why HHAT, which never touches the receptor, counts as a positive regulator of the pathway rather than a component of it. Substrate selectivity is essentially absolute for the Hedgehog N-terminal CGPGR motif.

Chitobiosyldiphosphodolichol beta-mannosyltransferase (EC 2.4.1.142): using GDP-mannose as donor, ALG1 transfers the first mannose onto the chitobiose core GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol via a beta-1,4 linkage to form Man1GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol, the first mannosylation step of dolichol-linked oligosaccharide (LLO) assembly, on the cytoplasmic face of the ER membrane. The product is the substrate for ALG2, the next enzyme in the pathway.
Contributes to ATP-driven proton pumping as a membrane-associated accessory component of V-ATPase, supporting endosomal and lysosomal acidification.

Binds extracellular renin and prorenin as a transmembrane receptor, mediating receptor-dependent ERK signaling and supporting angiotensin maturation by increasing receptor-associated renin catalytic efficiency. Renin performs angiotensinogen cleavage.

Activates BAP1 within PR-DUB and engages nucleosomal DNA to position monoubiquitinated histone H2A for BAP1-catalyzed hydrolysis. DNA and chromatin binding support this integrated noncatalytic activity.

Supports ligand-dependent RAR/RXR transcriptional coactivation through receptor association and cooperation with SRC-1. This receptor-coactivator role is distinguished from PR-DUB deubiquitinase activation; the supporting mouse expression assays and human receptor-binding fragments are separately scoped in the reference review.

NAD+-dependent 3-beta-hydroxy-Delta5-steroid dehydrogenase/isomerase that oxidizes the 3-beta-hydroxyl and isomerizes the Delta5 double bond of 7-alpha-hydroxylated C27 sterols (e.g. 7-alpha-hydroxycholesterol -> 7-alpha-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one), the second step of bile-acid biosynthesis.

Specific 3-beta-dehydrogenation of the 7-alpha-hydroxylated sterol cholest-5-ene-3-beta,7-alpha-diol (7-alpha-hydroxycholesterol), EC 1.1.1.181, the biochemically demonstrated bile-acid-precursor-specific activity of HSD3B7.

Signaling adaptor of TLR3 and of the endosomal (TRAM-dependent) arm of TLR4: engages the receptor TIR domain and recruits TRAF6, TRAF3, TBK1 and RIPK1 through distinct motifs; the TBK1-phosphorylated pLxIS motif recruits IRF3 for its activation, driving type I interferon production, while the TRAF6/RIPK1 branch activates canonical NF-kappaB.

DEPDC5 binds Rag GTPases and organizes their engagement with GATOR1 at the lysosomal surface. Its contacts with RagA regulate access to the catalytic module, while an auxiliary RagC interface helps coordinate nucleotide loading. DEPDC5 contributes to the complex's GAP activity and amino-acid-dependent suppression of mTORC1; NPRL2 supplies the catalytic arginine finger.

Contributes proton translocation in the assembled V-ATPase, coupling the complex's ATP-driven rotary mechanism to endosomal and Golgi acidification. ATP hydrolysis occurs in the V1 sector rather than autonomously in a2.

Binds phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate through the cytosolic N-terminal domain, helping target or retain a2 at Golgi membranes. Direct binding and localization experiments tested human a2 residues 1–400; the contribution to targeting of the full-length pump is a mechanistic inference.
Primary molecular function. CPT1C is a palmitoyl thioesterase (EC 3.1.2.22) with catalytic triad Ser-252, His-470, Asp-474. Demonstrated by mutagenesis studies in PMID:30135643.

MUTED stabilizes BLOC-1, supporting membrane-cargo delivery from endosomes to melanosomes and melanosome organization. Human MUTED complementation restores complex stability, pigmentation and cargo delivery in mutant mouse melanocytes.

Acts as a cyclin regulatory subunit that promotes CDK activity and supports the centriole-amplification program through which epithelial cells become multiciliated. The kinase partner operating in native multiciliated cells remains unresolved.

PNPLA3 hydrolyses acyl esters of glycerol at the lipid droplet surface using a Ser47/Asp166 catalytic dyad, acting on triacylglycerol, diacylglycerol and monoacylglycerol with a preference for oleate and for polyunsaturated acyl chains, and it can resolve the acyl-enzyme intermediate onto another acylglycerol instead of water, giving CoA-independent transacylation. The net job in a hepatocyte is fatty-acid-selective remodelling of the triacylglycerol pool rather than bulk lipolysis. The activity is stimulated by ABHD5/CGI-58, as ATGL's is, and is reduced roughly fivefold by the I148M substitution. Its quantitative importance in vivo is disputed - Pnpla3-null mice have no hepatic phenotype in one set of laboratories while another reports aggravated steatosis and reduced VLDL-triglyceride secretion on hepatic knockout.

On the lipid droplet surface PNPLA3 binds ABHD5/CGI-58, the obligatory co-activator of the major triglyceride lipase ATGL/PNPLA2, more avidly than ATGL does, and competes with ATGL for it; PNPLA3 recruits and retains ABHD5 on droplets more effectively than ATGL can. The consequence is reduced ATGL-mediated triglyceride hydrolysis, so the molecular activity is sequestration of a lipase activator and the functional outcome is lipase inhibition. This is a property of wild-type PNPLA3, not only of the variant - I148M and wild-type protein bind ABHD5 with similar characteristics - but the variant escapes ubiquitin-mediated degradation and reaches roughly fortyfold higher levels on hepatic droplets, which is what converts the activity into steatosis. Whether wild-type PNPLA3 at endogenous abundance measurably restrains ATGL in normal liver is not established, and this arm of PNPLA3 function is currently absent from GO annotation altogether.

LRRK2 contains a kinase domain that phosphorylates Rab GTPases at threonine residues in their switch II regions. Primary substrates include Rab8A (Thr72), Rab10 (Thr73), Rab12 (Thr73), and Rab29 (Thr71).
The ROC (Ras of complex proteins) domain of LRRK2 binds and hydrolyzes GTP. GTP binding and hydrolysis regulate kinase domain activity through intramolecular signaling.
LRRK2 ROC domain binds GTP, which is essential for regulating kinase activity. GTP binding status affects the conformation and enzymatic output of the protein.

Acts as an integral scaffold of the COG tethering complex, organizing COG-subunit contacts and coordinating Sly1 with syntaxin 5 to support Golgi retrograde trafficking and architecture. Human full-length and N-terminal constructs establish the recruitment mechanism; equivalent activity of the 337-residue Cog4S and N-terminally shortened 712-residue product has not been demonstrated.

Provides a COG5-contacting structural interface that assembles lobe B of the COG complex at Golgi membranes and supports resident-protein recycling, Golgi organization and protein maintenance. Human COG7 interface mutations impair COG5 association and recovered lobe-B assembly; COG7 loss reduces lobe-B partner abundance, and COG7 correction restores GS15 in patient cells. Stabilization is complex mediated, with the resident-protein turnover route unresolved. Yeast fragment structures and human COG5 rescue experiments have distinct scope; isolated COG7 tethering, SNARE bridging and enzymatic activity are not established.

Binds Golgi SNAREs, including STX16, as a subunit of the COG complex, coupling recognition to complex-dependent carrier capture and SNARE-complex organization. Human experiments establish COG8-dependent endosome-to-TGN transport and ectopic recruitment of STX16-bearing carriers, with lobe B retained in the retargeting context. Binding alone is insufficient for recruitment; COG8 is not itself a fusogenic SNARE or a demonstrated autonomous tether. Complex assembly and maintenance of Golgi organization are integrated aspects of this trafficking role.

Force-generating heavy chain of the single-headed inner dynein arms IDAb and IDAe in motile cilia and sperm flagella; its ATP-driven minus-end-directed motor activity contributes to axonemal doublet sliding and thus to beating of respiratory cilia and the sperm flagellum.

Structural subunit required for assembly of the inner dynein arms of the sperm axoneme; without DNAH7, IDAs and the other IDA heavy chains DNAH3 and DNAH6 are lost from sperm flagella while outer arms remain.
DDX41 binds RNA and associates with activated nuclear spliceosomes, supporting pre-mRNA splicing and its coordination with transcriptional elongation.

DDX41 couples ATP hydrolysis to DNA duplex unwinding and also promotes ATP-independent strand annealing. Its DNA-binding and remodeling capacities contribute to cytosolic DNA-triggered cGAS/STING signaling.

Membrane-associated CRB2 supplies a C-terminal PDZ-binding motif and a separate FERM-interaction region to the epithelial polarity system, supporting apical junction organization and maintenance. Direct human RPE depletion particularly impairs maintenance and recovery after junction disruption; developmental mouse retinal evidence adds tissue-organization context. Direct PDZ specificity is measured for the CRB2 1276–1285 peptide against isolated PDZ domains in PMID:36115835; the literal partner constructs are retained in the evidence index. PMID:38570189 separately detects MPP5 in the human CRB2–porcine retinal pull-down network and supplies target-specific complex context, not a direct PDZ-contact test. Neither result implies that every peptide-screen partner forms the same native complex. The FERM interaction is separately retained as domain-specific binding; the gamma-secretase-associated inhibitory pool is a positive contextual function outside this principal polarity unit. The predicted secreted second product lacks the canonical tail, and equivalent activity of product 3 is untested.

Catalytic subunit of the NatA complex catalyzing co-translational N-terminal (alpha-amino) acetylation of nascent polypeptides bearing small N-terminal residues (Ser, Ala, Thr, Gly, Cys, Val) exposed after initiator-methionine excision, using acetyl-CoA (EC 2.3.1.255).

As the catalytic component of the ribosome-associated NatA complex, NAA10 partners with the auxiliary subunit NAA15 (which anchors the enzyme to the ribosome) to act co-translationally on emerging nascent chains.
Binds dynein heavy-chain components as a noncatalytic outer-arm intermediate chain, organizing the motor complex during assembly and ciliary movement.
Binds dynein light-chain components as a complementary part of the outer-arm intermediate-chain assembly.

Organizes the BBSome subunit interface that supports selective membrane-protein trafficking at cilia and ciliary assembly or maintenance. BBS7 forms a coiled-coil heterodimer with BBS2; this pair joins BBS9 through a separate BBS2-BBS9 interface. Mouse loss-of-function experiments show reciprocal dependence of BBS7 and BBS2 protein stability and cargo-selective localization defects, including abnormal ciliary dopamine D1 receptor accumulation while several other receptors retain their ciliary localization. The complex associates with the ciliary membrane, with basal-body localization also supported by the inherited ortholog annotation. Zebrafish perturbation shortens Kupffer-vesicle cilia and mouse loss disrupts sperm flagellar axonemes. These context-dependent roles do not make BBS7 an autonomous cargo receptor, a transport motor, or a chaperonin catalyst.

Molecular chaperone / assembly factor for the F1 catalytic sector of mitochondrial ATP synthase (Complex V); binds the unassembled F1 alpha subunit (ATP5F1A) at the matrix face of the mitochondrial inner membrane and suppresses its non-productive aggregation, promoting formation of the alpha3-beta3 catalytic core. Non-catalytic.

Recognizes regulatory DNA through the conserved CG-1 domain and activates transcription in the nucleus. Human transactivation and mammalian CAMTA DNA-recognition evidence jointly support this activity; the native human target repertoire remains incompletely defined.

Non-catalytic assembly factor for mitochondrial respiratory-chain complex I. As a core subunit of the mitochondrial complex I intermediate assembly (MCIA) complex, NDUFAF1 associates with partner assembly factors and early membrane-arm intermediates to promote ND2-module assembly, then dissociates before formation of the mature holoenzyme. No autonomous molecular function has yet been resolved.

Mitochondrial matrix GTPase that binds and hydrolyzes GTP; its low intrinsic GTPase activity is strongly stimulated by methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (MMUT/MUT), which acts as a GAP. This nucleotide cycle powers MMAA's chaperone functions toward MMUT.

G-protein chaperone that, in a GTP-dependent manner, gates transfer of the adenosylcobalamin (AdoCbl) cofactor from the adenosyltransferase MMAB onto MMUT apoenzyme, protects the MMUT-bound cofactor from oxidative inactivation, and reactivates inactive MMUT by promoting exchange of the damaged cofactor. This maintains MMUT (and hence propionate/methylmalonyl-CoA) flux and is the process disrupted in cblA-type methylmalonic aciduria. MMAA is not itself the mutase and does not carry the cofactor as cargo; it regulates a gated protein-protein handoff.

MDA5 binds the internal stem of long double-stranded RNA and polymerises head-to-tail along it. Unlike RIG-I it reads duplex length rather than a terminal chemical mark, and it is the RNA-binding event that licenses everything downstream. The duplexes it engages in cells are not necessarily viral: iCLIP of endogenous MDA5 during SARS-CoV-2 and encephalomyocarditis virus infection recovers host transcripts, concentrated in introns and near inverted Alu repeats, which are themselves capable of base-pairing.

Duplex-RNA-stimulated ATP hydrolysis by the DExD/H helicase core. The ATPase does not act as a processive duplex unwindase; it drives the assembly and disassembly of MDA5 filaments, and this turnover is the proofreading step that makes signalling depend on duplex length. Helicase catalytic activity is dispensable for interferon induction by full-length MDA5, so the ATPase tunes rather than transmits the signal.

Ligand-activated innate immune receptor activity: ligand binding occurs in the cytosol, where filament assembly clusters the tandem CARDs; the clustered CARDs then nucleate MAVS polymers at the mitochondrial outer membrane and drive TBK1/IKBKE and IRF3/IRF7 activation, inducing interferon-alpha/beta. This is MDA5's defining role, and is recorded here with an explicit caveat: GO:0038187 is defined as combining with a pathogen-associated molecular pattern, and whether MDA5's activating ligand is pathogen-derived is unsettled. Viral mRNA lacking 2'-O-methylation and long viral duplexes activate it, but in infected cells the bound RNA is predominantly host, gain-of-function variants cause sterile interferonopathy, and ADAR1 editing exists to keep endogenous duplexes from triggering it.

Phosphotyrosine-dependent transmembrane scaffold of the TCR signalosome: once phosphorylated by ZAP70, LAT docks PLCG1, GRB2-SOS1, GRAP2-LCP2 and other SH2 effectors at the plasma membrane and nucleates the multiprotein complex that propagates T cell receptor signals to calcium and Ras-MAPK pathways.

Scaffold for phase-separated signaling condensates: multivalent phospho-LAT cross-linked by GRB2-SOS1 (and GADS-SLP-76-NCK) forms liquid-like membrane clusters that enrich kinases, exclude phosphatases and promote downstream signaling output.

The same adaptor function downstream of other ITAM-coupled receptors: FcepsilonRI in mast cells and the collagen receptor GPVI in platelets, where LAT is phosphorylated by SYK and is required for PLCgamma activation, calcium mobilization, degranulation and integrin activation.

Sigma-1C is the cargo-reading subunit of one of the three ubiquitous AP-1 variants. As part of the assembled tetramer on trans-Golgi and endosomal membranes it supplies the two adjacent hydrophobic pockets that receive the bulky residues of an acidic dileucine [DE]XXXL[LI] sorting signal, together with a basic patch that reads a phosphoserine just downstream of the motif, so that cargo selection can be tuned by phosphorylation. Bridging that captured cargo to the clathrin lattice is a property of the whole complex rather than of this subunit, which is why the clathrin-cargo adaptor activity is recorded as a contribution; what sigma-1C itself brings is the sorting-signal binding surface and a structural role in holding the tetramer together through its interface with the medium adaptin. Structural molecule activity is recorded as the subunit-level function because it is the only one GO can currently express for this protein: the activity it actually performs alone, binding the dileucine sorting signal, has no GO term and is proposed here as a new one.

Through the same complex, sigma-1C supports autophagosome formation. Autophagosome biogenesis depends on AP-1-mediated membrane traffic, and cells lacking AP1S3 make fewer autophagosomes on starvation, a defect reversed by wild-type but not by the assembly-defective p.Arg33Trp protein. The contribution is the same cargo-sorting activity applied to a different itinerary rather than a second, autophagy-specific function, and it is seen in HEK293 as well as in keratinocytes, so it is not a cell-type-restricted role.

As the obligatory subunit of the hexameric LRRC8 channel, LRRC8A forms the swelling-activated anion conduction pathway of the plasma membrane. The channel opens on hypotonic cell swelling or a fall in cytoplasmic ionic strength and releases chloride together with organic osmolytes, driving regulatory volume decrease. LRRC8A is pore-forming rather than accessory - a charged residue at the narrowest constriction of the LRRC8A homohexamer is a pore determinant of the heteromeric channel - but in cells it produces no current on its own and must co-assemble with LRRC8B, C, D or E, which set kinetics, conductance and substrate preference. Purified LRRC8A homohexamers do conduct anions in reconstituted systems. The activity is therefore recorded as a contribution to a complex-level function rather than as an activity LRRC8A independently enables. A second pool of the same channels operates on lysosomal membranes.

ATP-binding atypical UbiB-family kinase-like protein whose demonstrated catalytic activity is ATP hydrolysis (ATPase), gated by nucleotide binding that relieves KxGQ-mediated autoinhibition and stimulated by the COQ6:COQ3 pair. Acting at the matrix face of the inner mitochondrial membrane, it supports assembly and activity of the COQ synthome and streamlines coenzyme Q10 production; it is not a canonical in-trans protein kinase (an in vitro COQ3 phosphorylation is recorded as non-core).

OATP5A1 is a 12-transmembrane member of the organic anion transporting polypeptide (SLCO/SLC21) family that resides in the plasma membrane and, on family grounds, moves solutes by coupling to another solute gradient rather than to ATP hydrolysis. It was the last well-expressed orphan of the family, and its substrate profile has been reported only once, from a single laboratory using HEK293 cells overexpressing the protein: uptake of estrone-3-sulfate (Km 102 uM), L-tyrosine (Km 170 uM) and thiamine (Km 16 uM), together with efflux of glutamine and glycine, with pantothenic acid and thymine inhibiting tyrosine uptake. The molecular function is stated at this general level deliberately. The bidirectional profile is readily explained if OATP5A1 is an electroneutral exchanger, which would make the influx and efflux substrates two halves of one antiport cycle, but no counter-substrate or stoichiometry has been measured; and the flagship substrate, estrone-3-sulfate, was not transported in two earlier Xenopus oocyte studies, so the profile is demonstrably system-dependent. The specific substrate molecular functions are recorded in this review as reviewer proposals awaiting independent replication rather than as established activities.

ASPM binds microtubule minus ends at mitotic spindle poles, limiting minus-end growth and recruiting katanin to enhance microtubule severing in the conserved ASPM-katanin mechanism. This activity supports spindle organization and mitotic spindle orientation. Growth inhibition and recruitment-dependent enhancement of severing were demonstrated using purified short mouse ASPM with calmodulin; human endogenous association, minus-end recruitment and cellular perturbations support the conserved mechanism. ASPM supplies growth-blocking and recruitment functions, while katanin supplies ATP-dependent severing catalysis.
Catalyzes H3K36 mono- and dimethylation on nucleosomal chromatin, contributing to chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation.

IL23R is the IL-23-specific subunit of the heterodimeric IL-23 receptor. It binds IL-23 p19 through its N-terminal Ig domain and pairs with IL12RB1 (which binds IL-12 p40) to form the signaling-competent receptor complex. IL23R constitutively associates with JAK2 and, upon IL-23 binding, recruits STAT3, activating the JAK2/TYK2-STAT3 cascade that drives Th17 gene expression programs.

Central component of the NPHP (NPHP1-4-8) transition-zone module, located at the distal transition zone close to the membrane. It is an essential part of the ciliary barrier that controls membrane and soluble protein entry into the cilium, and it acts redundantly with the MKS module in transition-zone membrane attachment. No specific molecular activity has been defined.
At epithelial cell-cell junctions, NPHP4 is required with NPHP1 for timely tight-junction formation and apical organization during epithelial morphogenesis.

Protein serine/threonine kinase recruited by CEP164 to the distal appendages of the mother centriole, where it phosphorylates ciliogenesis substrates (CEP83, MPHOSPH9, CEP164) to trigger removal of the CP110-CEP97 cap, ciliary vesicle docking and IFT recruitment, thereby initiating primary cilium assembly.

DOCK6 promotes nucleotide exchange on Rho-family small GTPases, coupling their activation to cytoskeletal remodeling. Rac1/CDC42 exchange was reported in neuronal-cell studies, while human patient fibroblasts show altered actin organization. Human DOCK6 has a cytosolic pool and associates with LRCH proteins that can redistribute it. Activation depends on experimental context: a later human-cell FRET screen detected no Rac1/CDC42 activation under its tested conditions.

DOCK7 catalyzes guanine-nucleotide exchange on Rho-family GTPases. Purified human DHR2 fragments activate RAC1 and CDC42 when the GTPases are prenylated and associated with liposomes; the corresponding soluble, nonprenylated substrates show little or no exchange under those conditions. Axonal enrichment is reported in developing hippocampal neurons, where RAC signaling contributes to neuronal polarity. DOCK7 also has a cytosolic pool and can be recruited into membrane-associated signaling complexes.

DOCK7 also regulates microtubule growth through TACC3 independently of its nucleotide-exchange domain. In mouse cortical radial glial cells, its TACC3-binding region controls interkinetic nuclear migration and the balance between progenitor expansion and neuronal differentiation. Human neuroblastoma cells show endogenous DOCK7 and TACC3 colocalization at the centrosome.

DOCK8 promotes CDC42 nucleotide exchange through its DHR-2 domain, coupling localized CDC42 activation to leukocyte polarization and migration. Human DOCK8 constructs support CDC42 activation and regulated leading-edge recruitment in cell assays; the dendritic-cell migration and structural evidence includes mouse experiments. LRCH1 restrains access to CDC42, while PKCα-dependent phosphorylation promotes release of this inhibition.

DOCK8 provides signaling-adaptor activity in CpG-stimulated human B cells, associating with MyD88 and Pyk2 and supporting phosphorylation-dependent recruitment of Src-family kinases. This activity helps couple TLR9 stimulation to Pyk2–Src–Syk–STAT3 signaling. The assembly geometry and proposed SH2-binding interface remain unresolved.
ER-resident L-type lectin whose conserved carbohydrate-recognition domain binds high-mannose glycans (D-mannose), enabling recognition of glycoprotein cargo in the early secretory pathway.

Regulator of ER export of a subset of glycoproteins, acting as a lectin-type ER export receptor and as a regulator of ERGIC-53; knockdown slows glycoprotein secretion and overexpression redistributes ERGIC-53 to the ER.

ER-lumenal procollagen-proline 3-dioxygenase that catalyzes 3-hydroxylation of specific procollagen prolines (notably alpha1(I)Pro986) using a non-heme Fe(II) center, 2-oxoglutarate, O2 and L-ascorbate, a modification required for proper collagen folding.

Catalytic core of the ER collagen prolyl 3-hydroxylation (PCP) complex with CRTAP and PPIB/cyclophilin B, which binds, modifies and chaperones unfolded collagen and mutually stabilizes its components in the ER lumen.

Catalyses the terminal step of adenosylcobalamin (coenzyme B12) synthesis, transferring the 5'-deoxyadenosyl group from ATP to reduced cob(I)alamin to produce adenosylcob(III)alamin, and uses ATP as the adenosyl donor.

Binds cobalamin (in a base-off state) and, in an ATP-dependent manner, holds the AdoCbl product and delivers it directly to methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, functioning as a cobalamin-binding cofactor escort in the mitochondrial matrix.

BICC1 functions as an RNA-binding translational repressor. It contains three KH domains that bind specific stem-loop structures in target mRNA 3'UTRs, including Cripto-1, Pkd2, Dvl2, Wnt11b, and Dand5. BICC1 recruits the CCR4-NOT deadenylase complex to silence target transcripts. The SAM domain mediates self-polymerization and localization to cytoplasmic P-bodies where BICC1 forms oligomeric silencing platforms. Through regulation of Dvl2 and other Wnt pathway components, BICC1 negatively regulates canonical Wnt signaling. Evidence includes mRNA interactome capture (PMID:22658674), functional studies showing Wnt pathway regulation (PMID:21922595), and biochemical characterization of RNA binding (Zhang et al. 2014, PMC3953263).

Transfers the eighth mannose from Dol-P-Man in an alpha-1,6 linkage to Man7GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol at the lumenal face of the ER membrane, producing the Man8 precursor during assembly of the lipid-linked glycan used for protein N-linked glycosylation.

SOCS1 is a direct inhibitor of Janus kinase catalytic activity. It binds receptor- associated JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 (via its SH2 domain docking onto phosphotyrosine in the JAK activation loop, with its kinase inhibitory region (KIR) acting as a pseudosubstrate that blocks the kinase substrate-binding groove), markedly reducing JAK tyrosine-kinase activity and suppressing downstream STAT phosphorylation and activation.

SOCS1 binds activated Janus kinases through its SH2 domain, recognizing phosphotyrosine within the JAK JH1 (kinase) domain. This phosphotyrosine-dependent docking onto the activated kinase is the prerequisite for kinase inhibition and for delivering bound substrates to the ubiquitination machinery.

Through its C-terminal SOCS box, SOCS1 recruits the Elongin BC complex and a Cullin (CUL2/CUL5)/RBX1 scaffold to assemble an ECS (Elongin BC-Cullin-SOCS box) E3 ubiquitin ligase, acting as the substrate-recognition subunit that brings bound target proteins to the ligase for polyubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation (e.g. NF-kB RelA in the ECS(SOCS1) complex).
SH2-mediated docking of SOCS3 onto phosphotyrosine motifs of activated cytokine receptors and JAK2, positioning SOCS3 at the receptor/kinase complex.
KIR/SH2-mediated inhibition of JAK tyrosine kinase activity, blocking downstream STAT phosphorylation as the catalytic core of SOCS3 negative feedback.
Substrate-recognition subunit of an Elongin BC-Cullin5-RBX2 (ECS) E3 ubiquitin ligase that, via the SOCS box, targets bound receptor/JAK components for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.
Negative-feedback inhibition of cytokine receptor signaling through the JAK-STAT pathway, the integrative core role of SOCS3 (principal brake on IL-6/gp130 signaling).

Zinc-dependent C1 decarboxylase of the coenzyme Q head-group modification pathway. As a subunit of the mitochondrial CoQ biosynthetic complex (COQ synthome / metabolon), COQ4 catalyzes the decarboxylation of a 4-hydroxy-3-methoxy-5-(polyprenyl)benzoate intermediate to the corresponding 2-methoxy-6-(polyprenyl)phenol with release of CO2, a step required for CoQ10 biosynthesis. The activity requires a bound Zn2+ ion.

Binds a catalytic Zn2+ ion, coordinated by a conserved His/Asp/His/Glu motif (residues 163, 164, 167, 179), that is essential for COQ4's decarboxylase activity and for its ability to promote ubiquinone formation.

Catalyzes sn-1 deacylation of glycerophospholipids, including phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidate, generating 2-acyl lysophospholipids and free fatty acids. PI hydrolysis generates LPI and is modulated by PA; the physiological substrate range and relative contributions vary with cellular lipid context.

Catalyzes calcium-dependent nucleoside-diphosphate hydrolysis in the secretory pathway, with UDP turnover supporting proteoglycan glycosaminoglycan synthesis. The nucleotide-recycling model couples removal of luminal UDP to UMP production for nucleotide-sugar exchange; CANT1 does not transfer sugars to the glycan chain.

ISCA2 is a core component of the late-stage mitochondrial ISC pathway, functioning specifically in [4Fe-4S] cluster assembly. Biochemical reconstitution studies (PMID:25347204) demonstrated that the ISCA1:ISCA2 heterodimeric complex receives [2Fe-2S] clusters from GLRX5 and assembles them into [4Fe-4S] clusters through reductive fusion, with electrons supplied by FDX2/FDXR.

Contributes to extracellular matrix structural integrity and elastic fiber assembly through self-assembly and interactions with elastin and fibulins, including promotion of fibulin-4 matrix deposition.
Acts as an extracellular integrin ligand through its C-terminal globular C1q domain to mediate cell-matrix adhesion.

TRAPPC4 contributes a core subunit required for TRAPP complex assembly/stability, RAB1 guanine-nucleotide exchange, ER-to-Golgi trafficking, and autophagy. Its molecular role is best modeled as contribution to TRAPP complex GEF activity rather than independent catalysis.

Imports L-glutamate from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix across the mitochondrial inner membrane in electroneutral symport with a proton (H+/glutamate symport, or glutamate/OH- exchange), supplying matrix glutamate for catabolism, transamination, and ammonia handling.

Acts as the specific L-glutamate transmembrane transporter of the mitochondrial inner membrane; loss of this activity (e.g. the DEE3 variant Pro206Leu) causes developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 3.

NADPH-dependent all-trans-retinaldehyde reductase / all-trans-retinol dehydrogenase (EC 1.1.1.300): reduces all-trans-retinaldehyde to all-trans-retinol using NADPH in photoreceptor inner segments and other tissues.
NADPH-dependent 11-cis- (and 9-cis-) retinaldehyde reductase: reduces cis-retinaldehydes to the corresponding cis-retinols, part of the dual-substrate specificity of RDH12.
NADP(H) cofactor binding: RDH12 binds NADPH with high affinity (Km ~1.2 uM) and strongly prefers it over NAD(H) as the reducing cofactor.

Detoxification of reactive lipid-peroxidation aldehydes in photoreceptors: reduces 4-hydroxynonenal (and other C9 aldehydes) to nontoxic alcohols, protecting photoreceptors from light-induced oxidative injury.

Acetyl-CoA-dependent glucosamine 6-phosphate N-acetyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.4) that transfers an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to D-glucosamine 6-phosphate, producing N-acetyl-D-glucosamine 6-phosphate (GlcNAc-6-P) and CoA. This is the second committed step of the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway, feeding UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis. The enzyme acts as a homodimer with a GNAT fold and operates in the cytosol.

Cytochrome c is the soluble heme c electron carrier in the mitochondrial intermembrane space, accepting electrons from Complex III after ubiquinol oxidation and donating them to Complex IV for reduction of molecular oxygen.

After mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization, released cytochrome c binds APAF1 in the cytosol and contributes to assembly of the apoptosome that recruits and activates procaspase-9 in the intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway.

Secreted PCSK9 binds the EGF-A repeat of the hepatocyte LDL receptor and, after co-internalization, prevents receptor recycling so that LDLR is degraded in lysosomes; this non-catalytic activity lowers LDL clearance and raises plasma LDL cholesterol.

Autocatalytic intramolecular cleavage of the prodomain in the endoplasmic reticulum, which is required for PCSK9 maturation and secretion; the cleaved prodomain remains bound and blocks further catalysis.
Recognizes Sm-class pre-snRNAs (Sm site, 3' features and m7G cap) through its tandem WD40 propellers and delivers them to the SMN complex for Sm core assembly.
Binds the 7-methylguanosine cap of pre-snRNAs, contributing to snRNA selection.
Binds the SMN mRNA 3'-UTR and stimulates SMN translation.
Binds ribosomes (60S subunit) through its N-terminal region and dampens global protein synthesis.

Acts as a core TPR-superhelix subunit of the BBSome coat-like adaptor complex, mediating sorting and bidirectional trafficking of membrane/signaling proteins into and out of the primary cilium in coordination with ARL6/BBS3 and IFT.
Iron-sulfur cluster chaperone activity receiving [2Fe-2S] clusters from ISCU scaffold and transferring them to recipient apoproteins or [4Fe-4S] cluster assembly machinery in mitochondrial matrix
Regulation of heme biosynthesis in erythroid cells through control of ALAS2 translation via IRP1 iron-sulfur cluster status and ferrochelatase maturation

CHD8 supplies an ATP-driven nucleosome-remodeling motor. Purified human protein repositions nucleosomes and changes DNA accessibility, while DNA/histone contacts and recruitment by transcriptional partners connect the motor to locus-dependent activation and repression. Canonical Wnt repression and Pol III U6 regulation are established contexts. Repression need not be driven solely by the ATPase: tested mouse motorless short CHD8 recruits H1 and represses Wnt output independently of the ATPase domain. That construct result is distinct from human long-product motor assays. The H3K36me3/splicing connection remains a regulatory model rather than CHD8 methyltransferase or splicease chemistry. DNA/ATP engagement, beta-catenin recruitment and histone contacts are integrated targeting and substrate-recognition features of this core, rather than separate catalytic cores. The source-specific H3K4me3 fraction assay remains non-core and does not establish a second autonomous reader mechanism.
Facilitate cytoplasmic preassembly of outer and inner axonemal dynein arms by supporting heavy-chain incorporation and cooperation with the chaperone and assembly-factor machinery.
B3GLCT uses UDP-glucose to add beta-1,3-linked glucose to the O-fucose on folded TSR domains in the endoplasmic reticulum. This directly extends the glycan installed by POFUT2.

Non-catalytic mitochondrial inner-membrane assembly factor required for biogenesis of respiratory chain complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase); acts in MT-CO2 maturation / CuA copper-center formation together with the SCO1/SCO2/COA6 copper-delivery machinery and escorts the COX2 module onto the COX1-containing MITRAC intermediate.

Golgi membrane protein that binds GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase (GNPTAB), stabilising it and supporting its site-1 protease cleavage, activity and Golgi retention, and thereby is required for mannose 6-phosphate tagging and lysosomal delivery of soluble acid hydrolases.

C5-ring hydroxylation of the polyprenyl-benzoate intermediate of coenzyme Q biosynthesis: FAD-dependent, ferredoxin (FDX2/FDXR)-coupled monooxygenase that hydroxylates 4-hydroxy-3-(all-trans-decaprenyl)benzoate to 3,4-dihydroxy-5-(all-trans-decaprenyl)benzoate.

C1-hydroxylation step of coenzyme Q biosynthesis, acting downstream of COQ4: FAD-dependent, ferredoxin-coupled monooxygenase that hydroxylates 2-methoxy-6-(all-trans-decaprenyl)phenol to 2-methoxy-6-(all-trans- decaprenyl)benzene-1,4-diol, giving COQ6 a dual C5/C1 hydroxylase role.

Membrane-recruitment adaptor for the RasGAP neurofibromin: the EVH1 domain binds the NF1 GRD (GAPex) and the SPR domain anchors SPRED1 at the plasma membrane, positioning NF1 to inactivate Ras-GTP and thereby suppress growth-factor-induced Ras-ERK signalling (negative feedback). SPRED1 is non-catalytic and does not change NF1 GAP activity.

Secondary kinase-regulatory activity via the C-terminal cysteine-rich domain: direct inhibition of the cofilin kinase TESK1 (attenuating stress-fibre formation) and competition with substrates for the DYRK1A kinase domain.

Dolichyl-phosphate beta-glucosyltransferase (Dol-P-Glc synthase) that transfers glucose from cytosolic UDP-alpha-D-glucose onto dolichyl phosphate on the cytoplasmic face of the ER membrane, producing Dol-P-Glc, the lipid-linked glucose donor used by ALG6, ALG8 and ALG10 to complete the Glc3Man9GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol N-glycan precursor.

Binds a single [4Fe-4S] cluster via a conserved CXXC motif and acts as an ATP-binding Mrp/NBP35-family Fe-S carrier that delivers Fe-S cofactor(s) to respiratory Complex I subunits during their maturation in the mitochondrial matrix.
Binds a [4Fe-4S] iron-sulfur cluster, the cofactor that NUBPL carries and transfers; the cluster is coordinated by a conserved CXXC motif (Cys-244/Cys-247) required for Complex I assembly.

As the accessory/regulatory small subunit of the serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT) complex, SPTSSA is required for full SPT catalytic activity and sets the acyl-CoA chain-length specificity (favoring C16 palmitoyl-CoA), thereby driving the first, rate-limiting step of de novo sphingolipid biosynthesis in the ER membrane.

Structural accessory subunit of the membrane arm of mitochondrial respiratory chain Complex I; non-catalytic itself but a stable component required for assembly and stability of the membrane arm, contributing to the complex's NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase activity as part of mitochondrial electron transport from NADH to ubiquinone.

NDUFB11 (ESSS / Np17.3) acts as a non-catalytic structural subunit of the membrane (proximal) arm of mitochondrial respiratory chain Complex I. Imported via an N-terminal transit peptide and anchored in the mitochondrial inner membrane by a single transmembrane helix, it is a stable accessory subunit of the mature 45-subunit holoenzyme, required for its assembly and stability. It contributes to, but does not itself catalyze, the complex-level NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase activity.

ATP-dependent 5'-to-3' DNA helicase activity couples ATP hydrolysis-driven translocation to unwinding of DNA repair intermediates. BRIP1 contributes to homologous recombination through BRCA1-associated functions and to the interstrand-crosslink response through helicase activity and MLH1 binding. The latter response can be restored independently of BRCA1 binding; the exact helicase-controlled step in crosslink repair remains incompletely resolved.

ATP-dependent G-quadruplex unwinding resolves structured DNA obstacles encountered during replication and repair. RPA stimulates this activity, whereas MSH2/MSH6 inhibits it in the reported biochemical assays; cellular telomestatin sensitivity supports a genome-maintenance role without proving that every genomic G4 is a BRIP1 substrate.

ATP-driven BRIP1 motor activity unfolds a covalently DNA-bound protein adduct, exposing underlying DNA and enabling SPRTN to proteolyze the protein component. Purified human proteins support this mechanism; replication-coupled Xenopus experiments and selected translesion-synthesis reconstitutions define additional context-dependent roles. BRIP1 does not cleave DNA or replace SPRTN protease activity.

COA8 supports complex IV assembly and nascent-subunit stability at the matrix-facing inner membrane, including under oxidant challenge. Its molecular association with the heme O synthase COX10 is supported by controlled human cell co-immunopurification in an unreviewed 2024 preprint, and is therefore provisional. The W174A variant retains COX10 association and restores its abundance but fails to restore heme A and complex IV, separating binding from functional rescue. No intrinsic COA8 catalysis or purified COX10 rate enhancement has been demonstrated by these experiments.
Microsomal vitamin D 25-hydroxylase converting vitamin D3 and D2 to 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the first activation step of vitamin D and the main determinant of circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D

UFM1 is the covalent protein tag of the ufmylation system. After C-terminal processing to expose Gly-83, it is conjugated through an isopeptide bond to substrate lysines via the E1 (UBA5), E2 (UFC1) and E3 (UFL1/DDRGK1) cascade; it is the modifier, not an enzyme.

Through its conjugation, UFM1 participates in protein ufmylation, principally targeting the 60S ribosomal protein RPL26 on ER-bound ribosomes to support co-translational ER protein biogenesis and 60S subunit recycling from the ER.

Catalytic subunit of the ER-associated DHDDS–NUS1 cis-prenyltransferase complex. The substrate-binding active-site pocket lies in DHDDS, while the NUS1 C-terminal RxG motif contributes across the interface. This cooperative site catalyzes Mg2+-dependent extension of farnesyl diphosphate with isopentenyl diphosphate. The resulting unsaturated long-chain polyprenyl diphosphates provide precursors for dolichyl diphosphate and monophosphate biosynthesis; DHDDS does not perform the subsequent reduction or phosphorylation steps.

CHD7 couples ATP hydrolysis to nucleosome repositioning and altered DNA accessibility. This chromatin-remodeling activity supports context-dependent transcription and gene-expression regulation in nuclear chromatin. Nucleolar localization and rDNA occupancy add a ribosomal-gene regulatory context, while the exact remodeling step at rDNA remains a mechanistic model.

Imports cytosolic S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) into the mitochondrial matrix in antiport exchange for S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH), acting as the SAM:SAH antiporter of the mitochondrial inner membrane. This supplies SAM as the methyl donor for matrix methyltransferases.
Transports S-adenosyl-L-methionine across the mitochondrial inner membrane; SAMC is the only known route for SAM entry into mitochondria.

Calcium-regulated, electroneutral antiport of cytosolic adenine nucleotides (principally ATP-Mg, also ADP/AMP) for matrix inorganic phosphate across the mitochondrial inner membrane, setting the matrix adenine-nucleotide pool.
Broad-specificity adenine-nucleotide:phosphate antiport (ATP:phosphate and ADP:phosphate exchange), the specific mechanistic activity of the carrier domain measured by reconstitution.
Calcium binding by the N-terminal regulatory EF-hand domain facing the intermembrane space; the calcium sensor that gates the transporter, switching it on when cytosolic calcium rises.

Rate-limiting, BH4/ferrous-iron/O2-dependent hydroxylation of L-tryptophan to 5-hydroxy-L-tryptophan (5-HTP) — the first, committed step of serotonin biosynthesis (EC 1.14.16.4) — carried out in the cytosol of serotonergic (raphe) and enteric neurons.
Binding of a mononuclear non-heme ferrous iron (Fe2+) in the catalytic domain, required to activate molecular oxygen for tryptophan hydroxylation.

ARMC9 coordinates TOGARAM1 and CSPP1 through distinct partner-binding regions, contributing to cilium formation and stability. Its H region supports dimerization, although dimerization is not established as a requirement for every interaction. Partner recruitment and modulation of microtubule dynamics support adaptor activity in a flexible protein network. The precise cellular site of this activity remains unresolved: basal-body, daughter-centriole and conditional ciliary-tip distributions establish protein localization without locating each biochemical interaction. ARMC9 does not autonomously bind microtubules or supply polymerase activity in the tested reconstitution.

RING-type E3 ubiquitin ligase that, in partnership with the cognate E2 enzyme UBE2T, catalyzes site-specific monoubiquitination of FANCD2 (Lys561) and FANCI (Lys523) as the catalytic subunit of the Fanconi anemia core complex, activating the interstrand crosslink (ICL) repair pathway on chromatin.
Recruits and activates the dedicated E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBE2T via its C-terminal RING-type zinc finger, selecting UBE2T over other E2s to enable FANCD2/FANCI monoubiquitination.

PI3P-dependent recruitment and membrane remodeling by spastizin as part of the AP5-SPG11-SPG15 machinery, supporting autophagic lysosome reformation, lysosomal tubulation/membrane organization, membrane bending, and autophagosome maturation.

In mouse neurons, Lrig2 binds Neogenin and prevents premature ADAM17-mediated Neogenin ectodomain shedding. RGMa weakens the interaction to permit cleavage, and this control contributes to neurite-growth inhibition and cortical-neuron migration. The exact-ortholog transfer supports a conserved LRIG2 function, but direct human Neogenin binding, shedding control, and neuronal outputs remain untested.

Binds EGFR through the LRIG2 ectodomain and, in human glioblastoma models, increases EGFR abundance and activation and downstream PI3K/Akt signaling. Both plasma-membrane full-length LRIG2 and a released soluble ectodomain can perform this interaction; positive pathway regulation is established in engineered U87/U251 cells and is not assumed to operate with the same direction in normal human tissues.

Binds PDGFRB and positively modulates PDGFRB abundance, activation, and downstream Akt/STAT3 signaling in human U87 glioblastoma cells. This receptor-specific activity is bounded to the tested tumor context because mouse embryonic fibroblasts did not show corresponding effects on PDGFR abundance or phosphorylation.

Binding to DNA-binding regulators, including BCL6, recruits BCOR for repression of RNA polymerase II transcription. BCOR connects this recruitment to a PCGF1-containing PRC1.1 chromatin-modifying assembly and can associate with selected HDACs. It contributes to the ubiquitin-transferase activity of the assembled complex; RNF2 supplies the catalytic activity.
BLOS3 participates in the BLOC-1 assembly that organizes endosomal cargo delivery to melanosomes and supports platelet dense-granule biogenesis.

Cytosolic nucleotide-heptose sensing coupled to TIFA phosphorylation. Direct ADP-heptose recognition by the N-terminal domain activates the alpha-kinase domain, initiating TIFA-dependent innate signaling and canonical NF-κB activation. Thr9 is the well-resolved TIFA acceptor; the broad kinase class is used without asserting unresolved serine-specific chemistry. Downstream ubiquitination and TAK1/IKK catalysis belong to the partner enzymes.

Couples extracellular matrix attachment to the actin cytoskeleton through a membrane receptor and actin-binding cytoplasmic tail, supporting adhesion-dependent spreading and protrusive membrane organization.

Binds and bundles actin filaments through the cytoplasmic tail, providing a structural link between the membrane receptor and the actin cytoskeleton. Purified human tail residues 360–420 bind human beta-actin, with the Y383A substitution disrupting the interaction; this does not establish actin polymerization.

Mitochondrial complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) assembly factor that acts together with NDUFAF3 to build and anchor an early membrane-arm assembly intermediate; it is not a structural subunit of the holoenzyme and has no catalytic activity, functioning through protein-protein interactions with NDUFAF3, TIMMDC1 and nascent complex I subunits at the mitochondrial inner membrane.

Non-catalytic subunit of the ER-membrane cis-prenyltransferase (dehydrodolichyl diphosphate synthase) complex; with the catalytic subunit DHDDS it condenses isopentenyl diphosphate units onto farnesyl diphosphate to produce dehydrodolichyl diphosphate, the committed step of dolichol biosynthesis that provides the dolichol-phosphate glycan carrier for N-linked protein glycosylation in the ER. NUS1 has no activity alone but is required for and contributes to the complex activity via its C-terminal RXG motif (substrate binding) and stabilizes DHDDS.

ER-membrane DnaJ/Hsp40-type co-chaperone of the Sec61 translocon whose luminal J-domain recruits and stimulates the ATPase activity of the ER Hsp70 BiP (HSPA5) to drive translocation of precursor polypeptides into the ER lumen.
Auxiliary subunit of the SEC62-SEC63 complex of the ER translocon that supports cotranslational and post-translational import of precursor polypeptides into the endoplasmic reticulum.

RING-type E3 ubiquitin ligase that binds the N-box and C-box epitopes of Notch ligand (JAG1, DLL) cytoplasmic tails and transfers ubiquitin to them, marking ligands for epsin-dependent endocytosis that is required for Notch activation in the neighbouring cell.

DSE catalyzes manganese-dependent C5 epimerization of glucuronic acid residues within chondroitin chains, producing iduronic-acid-containing regions of dermatan sulfate. This same chemical step directly modifies chondroitin proteoglycan chains and contributes to dermatan-sulfate proteoglycan biosynthesis, as shown by human recombinant activity and cellular chain-composition measurements. The glycosylated catalytic domain acts in the secretory pathway; the core location follows the target-resolved Golgi reaction compartment, while the positive ER-associated protein pool is retained separately.

CILK1 is a serine/threonine kinase that enters cilia and concentrates at the ciliary tip, where it phosphorylates the kinesin-2 subunit KIF3A and regulates IFT turnaround and transport, so controlling ciliogenesis, cilium length and ciliary localization of Hedgehog pathway components.

Activating subunit of an ABI1-scaffolded EPS8L2-ABI1-SOS1 complex: the EPS8L2 effector region engages SOS1 and switches it to Rac-GEF activity, coupling growth factor receptor signalling to Rac activation and membrane ruffling. Experimentally established for human EPS8L2.

Direct binding of actin filaments through the conserved C-terminal effector region, which targets EPS8L2 to F-actin-rich ruffles (human, experimental) and, by orthology to same-subfamily mouse Eps8l2, to the tips of the shorter rows of hair-cell stereocilia, where it is needed to maintain the hair-bundle staircase.

Erases serine-linked mono-ADP-ribosylation. ADPRS hydrolyses the alpha-O-glycosidic bond between the anomeric C1'' of ADP-ribose and the serine hydroxyl of proteins modified by the PARP1/2:HPF1 complex, and is the only human enzyme known to do so. It acts on chromatin in the nucleus, where it is recruited to sites of DNA damage through recognition of ADP-ribose itself. Catalysis requires the two magnesium ions of the binuclear centre (GO:0000287, annotated separately by IDA): MgA positions the scissile linkage and MgB contributes to substrate binding. The metal is treated here as a property of the catalytic centre rather than as a core function in its own right - ADPRS is not interesting as a magnesium-binding protein.

Degrades protein-free poly(ADP-ribose), and is the dominant PAR-degrading activity of the mitochondrial matrix, where the alternatively spliced PARG isoform is catalytically inactive. Clearing free PAR limits the release of apoptosis-inducing factor from mitochondria and the parthanatic cell death it triggers.

Hydrolyses 1''-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose, the metabolite generated by sirtuin-catalysed histone deacetylation, releasing ADP-ribose and acetate. The authors report this reaction as significantly faster than the same enzyme's hydrolysis of poly(ADP-ribose) without quantifying the ratio; the widely repeated 250-fold figure from the same paper is a different comparison, ARH3 against ARH1 on O-acetyl-ADP-ribose. Either way the activity places ADPRS at the junction of ADP-ribose signalling and NAD+-dependent deacetylation. Like the other two activities it is magnesium-dependent.

ELOVL5 catalyzes the rate-limiting condensation step of the VLCFA elongation cycle, condensing acyl-CoA substrates with malonyl-CoA to produce 3-ketoacyl-CoA intermediates (EC 2.3.1.199). This is the first of four enzymatic steps in the ER-localized elongation cycle that adds two carbons per cycle.

ELOVL5 preferentially elongates C18-C20 polyunsaturated fatty acids of both n-3 and n-6 series. Key substrates include gamma-linolenic acid (18:3n-6), alpha-linolenic acid (18:3n-3), stearidonic acid (18:4n-3), arachidonic acid (20:4n-6), and EPA (20:5n-3). This activity is essential for endogenous synthesis of longer-chain PUFAs that serve as membrane lipid components and eicosanoid/docosanoid precursors.

ELOVL5 elongates intermediates in n-3 and n-6 PUFA biosynthesis pathways. It converts alpha-linolenic acid-derived intermediates toward EPA and DHA synthesis, and gamma-linolenic acid to DGLA in the n-6 pathway. Loss-of-function mutations reduce serum AA and DHA levels, confirming the essential role in these pathways.

Modulates transcription through interactions with nuclear-receptor/p160 coregulators, p53-associated cofactors and chromatin regulatory proteins. Repression or activation depends on partner and promoter context. ANKRD11 provides regulatory protein interactions; associated enzymes perform histone and transcription-factor modification.

Anchors the E3 dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase (DLD) dimer to the E2 (DLAT) core of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex via its E3-binding (peripheral subunit-binding) domain, acting as a molecular adaptor that tethers the catalytic E3 to the assembled complex; this structural role is essential for a functional PDC.

Serves as a structural constituent of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex inner core, integrating (together with E2/DLAT) into the dodecahedral core that provides the scaffold binding the peripheral E1 and E3 catalytic components; PDHX itself is non-catalytic (its E2-like inner-core fold lacks the catalytic histidine).
Cytosolic double-stranded DNA sensor: directly binds aberrant/foreign dsDNA as the input for innate immune activation.
DNA-activated nucleotidyltransferase that synthesizes the second messenger 2',3'-cGAMP from ATP and GTP (EC 2.7.7.86), initiating cGAS/STING signaling and type I interferon production.
Forms DNA-induced biomolecular condensates (liquid-like droplets) in which cGAS is concentrated with substrates and becomes catalytically active; cGAS is the scaffold of these condensates.

Binds and activates ATGL/PNPLA2 at lipid droplets, accelerating hydrolysis of stored triglycerides and maintaining neutral-lipid balance. A soluble cytosolic pool and regulated access to droplet-associated partners support this function. ABHD5 provides the regulatory activity; ATGL supplies the triglyceride-hydrolysis chemistry.

Promotes PNPLA1 recruitment and stimulation at lipid droplets during epidermal omega-O-acylceramide synthesis. Human construct experiments separate deficient ABHD5–PNPLA1 association from defective perilipin-dependent droplet targeting; forced membrane co-localization rescues the tested disease variants in proteoliposomes. ABHD5 provides spatial and regulatory support while PNPLA1 catalyzes transacylation. The effects depend on the reconstitution context, and this role is not expressed as intrinsic ABHD5 acyltransferase or lipase activity.

With IFT81, IFT74 forms the tubulin-binding module of IFT-B; its basic N-terminus binds the beta-tubulin C-terminal tail and greatly increases the affinity of the module for tubulin, supporting tubulin transport for axoneme extension and ciliogenesis.

Hydrolyzes the 5-phosphate of PI(4,5)P2 in the ciliary membrane, generating PI(4)P and confining PI(4,5)P2 to the ciliary base; this lipid identity restricts ciliary TULP3/GPR161 and permits Hedgehog signalling.
Hydrolyzes the 5-phosphate of PI(3,4,5)P3 with high affinity, limiting PI3K-derived signalling lipids and contributing to the stability of pre-formed primary cilia.

Associates with protein-folding chaperones while supporting cytoplasmic preassembly of outer and inner axonemal dynein arms with DNAAF2 and other assembly factors. Human-cell HSP70/HSP90 associations and mouse tissue chaperone co-immunoprecipitation support the binding function; they do not establish an autonomous folding reaction or a purified direct interface. DynAP localization is supported by tagged Xenopus ortholog experiments.

Promotes mitochondrial complex I assembly as a core MCIA component required for the stability of other assembly factors and formation of the ND2-module at the inner membrane. ACAD9 binds ECSIT; ECSIT connects it to NDUFAF1 and induces deflavination.

Catalyzes FAD-dependent dehydrogenation of long-chain fatty acyl-CoA substrates at the first step of mitochondrial beta-oxidation. This includes experimentally tested unsaturated C16-C22 substrates. The enzymatic state is inhibited by ECSIT binding and FAD release. Human-cell knockout/rescue evidence supports a physiological FAO contribution, whose magnitude depends on cellular context; a single assay ratio relative to VLCAD is not a universal measure of importance.

As the targeting subunit of the ATG12-ATG5-ATG16L1 complex, promotes covalent attachment of ATG8-family proteins to membrane phospholipid, the E3-like step of the ATG8 conjugation cascade. ATG16L1 supplies membrane placement and complex oligomerization rather than catalysis, so the activity belongs to the complex it completes.

Brings the ATG12-ATG5 conjugate to a membrane. ATG12-ATG5 alone does not bind membrane; ATG16L1 supplies two separable membrane-binding regions, an N-terminal one required for lipidation under all conditions and a beta-isoform-specific C-terminal one required only on perturbed endosomes, and this is what selects which bilayer is modified.

Through its WD40 C-terminal domain, directs lipidation of ATG8-family proteins onto single, pre-existing endolysosomal and endosomal membranes - the non-canonical or CASM arm. This is domain-separable from canonical autophagy, which does not need the WD40 domain, and it is the activity that underlies LC3-associated phagocytosis and the protective response to influenza A virus in mice.

Jouberin supports ciliary organization and vesicular cargo trafficking from the basal-body/transition-zone region as an MKS-complex-associated protein. Conserved cilium assembly includes motile and non-motile systems; the individual experimental models do not establish activity in every native human ciliated tissue. Mouse Ahi1 depletion disrupts Golgi-directed vesicle transport and transferrin recycling, while human fibroblast and construct assays establish ciliary cargo organization.
