Both assembly terms are listed because the requirement is flagellum-wide, not axoneme-only: CFAP58-deficient sperm show mitochondrial-sheath malformation and HSP60 depletion in the midpiece, where CFAP58 is concentrated, alongside the axonemal (central pair and radial spoke) defects, so sperm flagellum assembly (GO:0120316) covers a requirement that sperm axoneme assembly (GO:0007288) alone does not. Whether the midpiece contribution is direct or secondary to axonemal failure is unresolved, which is why sperm mitochondrial sheath assembly (GO:0120317) itself is kept as non-core.

CFAP43 supplies part of the tether/tether-head structure with CFAP44 along axonemal doublet microtubules in motile cilia and sperm flagella. Native human respiratory-axoneme models identify the canonical-sequence protein in conserved inner-dynein-arm docking machinery. In Tetrahymena, removing FAP43 destabilizes the position of retained I1 motor domains; mouse respiratory cilia can remain grossly assembled while Cfap43 loss changes beat frequency and transport. These complementary structural and functional observations support a conserved mechanical contribution to coordinated beating, including frequency modulation, rather than an intrinsic motor or kinase activity. The precise frequency-setting mechanism has not been isolated in human. Sperm axoneme organization and sperm movement are tissue manifestations of this structural role; severe sperm architecture defects do not imply universal failure of cilium initiation.

Binds centriolar microtubules through its N-terminal region and supports the construction and elongation of centrioles. Partner interactions and recruitment of distal components help build appendages and basal-body architecture competent for ciliogenesis; mouse quiescent-cell experiments additionally show context-dependent restraint of PCM accumulation.

Core structural component of the central-apparatus bridge of the motile axoneme: binds the C1 microtubule through its N-terminal domains, HYDIN through its central CFAP47-ring, and the C2 microtubule through its C-terminal region, tethering the two central microtubules; required for sperm axoneme assembly and sperm motility, and its loss causes X-linked MMAF (SPGFX3).

Binds the central microtubules directly: ASH1 and ASH4 contact protofilaments 13 and 1 of C1 (reinforcing the C1 seam) and ASH20 contacts protofilament 12 of C2; these microtubule contacts are what allow CFAP47 to tether C1 to C2.
Organizes ciliary and cytoplasmic protein complexes by linking NEK8 with INVS and NPHP3 and by remodeling ANKS3-containing assemblies. ANKS3 mediates the association with BICC1.
Promotes NEK8 kinase activation through an ankyrin-repeat-dependent interaction within the ciliary inversin compartment.

COX18 is a mitochondrial inner-membrane protein insertase (OXA1/ALB3/YidC family) that translocates the C-terminal tail of the newly synthesised core subunit MT-CO2 (COX2) across the inner membrane from the matrix side, acting after COX20- mediated stabilisation and before SCO1/SCO2/COA6 copper metallation, and is thereby required for cytochrome c oxidase (respiratory chain complex IV) assembly.

Acts as a membrane adaptor by coupling phosphoinositide recognition to recruitment and organization of APC, Axin and associated Wnt signaling proteins. Distinct complexes support negative downstream regulation and positive receptor-level regulation. Membrane targeting and protein-recruitment experiments support an active scaffolding role; the associated enzymes perform phosphorylation, ubiquitination and proteolysis.

Binds PtdIns(4,5)P2 through its N-terminal membrane-targeting region, anchoring AMER1 to the cytoplasmic plasma-membrane surface where it recruits Wnt signaling proteins. This lipid-recognition activity provides the membrane-targeting component of the adaptor mechanism.

Complex I-specific assembly factor with an FAD-dependent oxidoreductase fold. FOXRED1 is required for the mid-late stage of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) biogenesis, transiently associating with complex I subunits; without it a late (~815 kDa) intermediate fails to mature to the holoenzyme and breaks down to a ~475 kDa subcomplex, leaving only residual complex I. It is not a subunit of the mature enzyme, so NADH dehydrogenase activity is deliberately NOT assigned. Its molecular activity is captured only at the generic oxidoreductase level (DAO/FAD-NAD(P)-binding family, EC 1.-.-.-): no substrate or reaction is known, and the original description of FOXRED1 as a "molecular chaperone" rests on its assembly requirement, not on a demonstrated protein-folding activity, so protein folding chaperone (GO:0044183) is not assigned.

FAD (flavin adenine dinucleotide) binding. FOXRED1 is a flavoprotein whose FAD/NAD(P)-binding fold binds an FAD cofactor (by similarity), consistent with its Flavoprotein/FAD keywords. This molecular function is not currently in GOA; it is added here on the basis of the UniProt COFACTOR annotation and the DAO/FAD-binding domain architecture.

Non-catalytic inner-membrane assembly chaperone/scaffold that mediates incorporation of the core catalytic subunit MT-CO2 (COX2) into cytochrome c oxidase (respiratory chain complex IV). COX20 binds and stabilises newly synthesised MT-CO2 during membrane insertion and presents it to the SCO1/SCO2 metallochaperones for CuA copper delivery, driving cytochrome c oxidase assembly.

Hsp70-partner activity in cytoplasmic 60S subunit maturation: DNAJC21 associates with HSPA8, PA2G4 and ZNF622 in nuclease-treated human lysates, and the P32A HPD-loop mutation selectively impairs HSPA8 association. DNAJC21 loss perturbs PA2G4 traffic, with excess PA2G4 in 60S/80S fractions of affected-individual cells; wild-type re-expression restores that traffic. Together, these observations support a co-chaperone/assembly-factor contribution to large-subunit biogenesis. They do not directly measure human HSPA8 ATPase stimulation or reconstituted PA2G4 release, establish a purified binary interface, or define fixed complex stoichiometry.

RNA association during ribosome biogenesis: DNAJC21 associates with precursor 45S rRNA in nuclear extracts and occupies a nucleolar pool. Independent UV-dependent mRNA capture supports RNA-contact capacity, while the native rRNA co-IP does not establish purified sequence-specific recognition or RNA cleavage.

Directly inhibits the actin-capping-protein heterodimer through noncovalent binding, reducing CP-mediated barbed-end capping and promoting uncapping in purified CBR assays. Membrane and vimentin-associated localization coordinates this regulation with polarized protrusions; direct binary binding to vimentin is not established. The existing molecular-function inhibitor term captures the demonstrated activity, while the proposed CP-specific child term supplies its missing target specificity. CARMIL2 modulates CP activity rather than eliminating every CP function, and collective migration can be rescued independently of CP binding.

Organizes noncatalytic coupling of CD28 co-stimulation to CARD11-dependent NF-kappaB signaling in lymphocytes. This gene-level function is supported for signaling-competent splice forms, including the predominant 1399-residue leukocyte form described in PMID:36515678; the longest 1435-residue form did not rescue that pathway in the tested system. The immune-adaptor role is separable from CP binding. Signaling-complex association does not establish every direct binary contact or membership in the CARD11-BCL10-MALT1 complex.

Binds phospholipids, with phosphatidic acid and cardiolipin preferences inferred for human CFAP418 from full-length mouse ortholog overlay assays. Cytoplasmic and photoreceptor inner-segment localization provides the cellular context; the physiological membrane mechanism remains unresolved.

IBA57 forms a 2Fe-2S-bridged heterocomplex with ISCA2. Structural and biophysical studies demonstrate that Cys259 of IBA57 coordinates the bridging 2Fe-2S cluster (PMID:30269484). The C259A mutation abolishes complex formation. The 2Fe-2S cluster serves as an intermediate in 4Fe-4S cluster assembly through a reductive coupling mechanism with ISCA1 and ISCA2.

GTPase-activating protein for the Rag GTPases RagC and RagD, acting as the FLCN-FNIP1/2 heterodimer. FLCN supplies the catalytic arginine (Arg164); the activity is held off in the starvation-induced lysosomal folliculin complex and released on amino acid refeeding. It converts RagC/D to the GDP-bound state needed for substrate-specific mTORC1 phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention of TFEB/TFE3.
Uncompetitive inhibitor of lactate dehydrogenase A that binds LDHA directly and restrains glycolytic flux (a single-laboratory finding, non-core relative to the Rag GAP function).

Catalyzes transbilayer phospholipid scrambling in calcium-stimulated cell assays. Human constructs support surface lipid exposure, and endothelial ANO5 contributes to phosphatidylserine externalization. The plasma-membrane location describes where this surface lipid-exposure activity was measured; it does not exclude the substantial ER pool. Muscle membrane repair is also an established, biologically central ANO5 role. It is not assigned as a direct consequence of this molecular activity because a scrambling-defective chimera rescues repair. A separate repair activity cannot yet be named from the available experiments: annexin organization and calcium handling are implicated, but ANO5 has not been shown to execute a specific binding, scaffolding, transport or fusion step that explains repair.

STING1 is the signal-transducing adaptor of the cytosolic DNA-sensing pathway. Binding of 2'3'-cGAMP or of bacterial cyclic dinucleotides to its cytosolic ligand-binding domain triggers high-order oligomerisation and ER exit; at the ERGIC and Golgi the oligomer recruits TBK1 through its C-terminal PXPLRXD motif, is phosphorylated on Ser366, and the phosphorylated tail then recruits IRF3 for TBK1-dependent phosphorylation, driving type I interferon transcription. From post-Golgi endolysosomes the same adaptor activity engages TRAF6 and activates NF-kappaB.

STING1 is the intracellular receptor for 2'3'-cGAMP. The mixed 2'-5'/3'-5' linkage of the endogenous cGAS product is bound with far higher affinity than other cyclic GMP-AMP isomers, and binding closes the lid of the ligand-binding domain to initiate the conformational change that leads to oligomerisation. The same pocket binds bacterial cyclic di-GMP directly (GO:0035438), so STING1 serves as a sensor of bacterial cyclic dinucleotides as well as a receiver of the host second messenger.

The STING1 transmembrane domain forms a proton-conducting pathway at the interface between protomers. Purified STING1 reconstituted into liposomes supports transmembrane proton transport, and in cells its activation raises Golgi pH. The resulting proton efflux drives an output branch that is separable from interferon induction: non-canonical LC3B and GABARAP lipidation, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and relief of mTORC1 inhibition leading to TFEB/TFE3-driven lysosome biogenesis. The agonist C53 binds the channel interface and blocks flux, uncoupling these outputs from IRF3 signalling.

STING1 binds PtdIns(3,5)P2 through a groove formed at the interface between adjacent dimers, contributed by H16 and K20 of the N-terminal tail of one protomer and R71 of a neighbouring loop. Binding requires the full-length protein including the transmembrane domain, and is enhanced by cholesterol, which occupies an adjacent position in the same interface (GO:0015485). The lipid acts as a molecular glue that, together with cGAMP, stabilises high-order oligomers and thereby permits ER exit and TBK1 activation; PIKFYVE, the kinase that makes PtdIns(3,5)P2, is constitutively bound to STING1, and its deletion or mutation of the lipid-binding residues blocks trafficking and signalling. PtdIns(4,5)P2 occupies the same site in vitro. This is an activation requirement gating the adaptor function rather than an independent output, and it rests on companion papers from a single research programme.

CPLANE scaffold subunit at the ciliary base. It recruits transition-zone proteins (SEPT2, NPHP1, MKS1) and, with INTU and FUZ, peripheral IFT-A subunits needed for cilium assembly. Its C-terminal tail binds phosphoinositides.

A cortical planar polarity effector. It recruits SEPT2 to actin filaments and the cell cortex, organizing the septin-actin cytoskeleton for cell-shape stability, polarized protrusion and directional migration.

Molecular chaperone / assembly factor for mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I. NDUFAF2 binds a large late-stage complex I assembly intermediate (containing subunits of both the matrix and membrane arms) at the mitochondrial inner membrane, stabilizing it and promoting efficient assembly of the holoenzyme, from which NDUFAF2 is then released. It is not a stable structural subunit and has no catalytic activity of its own.

BBIP1 is an integral BBSome scaffold that connects BBS4 and BBS8 and stabilizes the human complex architecture. Through this structural contribution, it participates in the complex’s ciliary receptor localization and cilium-assembly roles. The scaffold activity is distinct from the unresolved proposal that BBIP1 coordinates HDAC6 with BBS4.

Required non-catalytic subunit of the GPI-GnT complex that contributes to the phosphatidylinositol N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase activity catalysing the first step of GPI biosynthesis (GlcNAc transfer from UDP-GlcNAc to phosphatidylinositol), acting by direct binding to and regulation of the catalytic subunit PIGA in the ER membrane.

Early assembly factor for mitochondrial respiratory chain Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase). As a core component of the inner-membrane MITRAC complex, COX14 associates with newly synthesised MT-CO1 (COX1) and, with COA3 and other MITRAC/assembly components, couples MT-CO1 synthesis with its incorporation into the nascent enzyme, regulating and stabilising the early COX1-containing assembly intermediate. COX14 is non-catalytic and acts as a scaffolding/regulatory factor; no informative molecular-function term is assigned (GOA carries only bare protein binding and an over-interpreted 'protein folding chaperone' term).

TBCK is the catalytic subunit of a Rab GTPase-activating module that acts on RAB5 at the early endosome. Its TBC domain retains the arginine and glutamine fingers that TBC-family GAPs insert into the GTPase active site, and the recurrent pathogenic missense allele p.Arg511His replaces the arginine finger. Acting with PPP1R21 and FERRY3, TBCK stimulates GTP hydrolysis on RAB5 and thereby limits RAB5 residence on early endosomes; without it RAB5 stays GTP-loaded, early endosomes swell and their conversion to late endosomes is blocked. TBCK is also a subunit of the wider five-protein FERRY complex, a RAB5A effector that tethers mRNA and ribosomes to early endosomes, but TBCK itself makes no mRNA contacts. The pseudokinase and rhodanese-like domains that flank the TBC domain are both catalytically dead.

Serves as the membrane-anchoring, non-catalytic subunit of the ALG14-ALG13 UDP-N-acetylglucosamine transferase, recruiting the soluble catalytic subunit ALG13 to the cytoplasmic face of the ER membrane so the heterodimer can add the second (beta-1,4-linked) GlcNAc to GlcNAc-PP-dolichol during dolichol-linked oligosaccharide assembly for protein N-glycosylation.

DYNC2I2 binds the DYNLL1/DYNLL2 and DYNLRB1/DYNLRB2 light-chain module and, together with intermediate-chain and heavy-chain contacts, organizes the asymmetric dynein-2 motor assembly. These subunit interfaces contribute to minus-end-directed transport of ciliary components and the transport machinery that supports cilium assembly. Basal-body, ciliary-interior, axonemal-track-associated and modeled tip-turnaround pools are complementary parts of this mechanism; axonemal association does not mean membership in an axonemal dynein arm. DYNC2I2 does not independently supply the motor ATPase activity.

Within the same asymmetric dynein-2 assembly, the C-terminal WD-repeat propeller of DYNC2I2 contacts a DYNC2H1 heavy-chain tail and links the intermediate/light-chain block to that motor tail. This is a subunit-binding interface of the assembled motor.

DYNC2I2 associates with the complementary DYNC2I1 intermediate chain in the dynein-2 intermediate/light-chain block that connects the two heavy-chain tails. This records the partner-class interaction within the same assembly; complex capture does not by itself establish an isolated binary affinity.

Promotes Rab39A nucleotide exchange, enabling recruitment of HOPS components during autophagosome–lysosome fusion. This activity was demonstrated for purified C9orf72 alone and supported by cellular loss/rescue; it is kept distinct from substrate-dependent GAP activity and contested exchange activity of SMCR8-containing preparations. C9orf72 does not itself supply HOPS tethering or SNARE membrane fusion.

Positions small-GTPase substrate and stabilizes the C9orf72–SMCR8 complex, contributing to GTP hydrolysis. Human-complex structures and C9orf72 interface mutations establish this physical contribution; SMCR8 supplies the catalytic Arg147 finger. ARF1/5/6 are robust biochemical substrates, while Rab8A hydrolysis required more complex in the tested preparation. WDR41 recruits the complex to lysosomes, but the physiological substrate pools and whether catalysis occurs at the lysosome remain unresolved.

Recognizes active Rab1A as an effector and coordinates recruitment of the ULK1 initiation machinery during autophagosome assembly. This is a recruitment mechanism distinct from exchanging nucleotide on Rab39A and from hydrolysis promoted by the SMCR8 complex. Interaction and trafficking experiments support the regulatory work without assigning ULK1 kinase activity, stable holo-ULK1 membership, or Rab1A exchange to C9orf72.

Oxidizes D-2-hydroxyglutarate to 2-oxoglutarate in mitochondria, using tightly bound FAD and a zinc-coordinating substrate pocket. This limits D-2-hydroxyglutarate accumulation. Strong D-malate and weaker D-lactate oxidation are measured additional substrate activities; their physiological contributions and the terminal electron acceptor remain unresolved.
Transfers phosphocholine from phosphatidylcholine to ceramide at the plasma membrane and Golgi, producing sphingomyelin and diacylglycerol and maintaining membrane sphingomyelin pools.

TMEM67 (meckelin) acts as a receptor for non-canonical Wnt signaling by directly binding WNT5A through its extracellular cysteine-rich domain (CRD), which is homologous to Frizzled/ROR receptors. It cooperates with ROR2 as a co-receptor to mediate non-canonical Wnt signaling that controls basal body positioning and epithelial branching morphogenesis. TMEM67 is essential for phosphorylation of ROR2 upon WNT5A stimulation. Recent work (DOI:10.1101/2024.09.04.611229) shows that ADAMTS9 proteolytic cleavage of TMEM67 generates a functional partition: the released N-terminal ectodomain is proposed to modulate Wnt signaling, while the C-terminal fragment supports TZ assembly. Cleavage-deficient TMEM67 mice retain apparently normal Wnt signaling while showing severe ciliogenesis/TZ phenotypes, supporting mechanistic separability of Wnt-related and TZ-related functions.

The cytoplasmic domain of TMEM67 directly interacts with filamin A (FLNA) at the apical cell surface associated with the basal body. This interaction mediates ciliogenesis and basal body positioning. Loss of filamin A phenocopies meckelin loss, causing basal body positioning and ciliogenesis defects. TMEM67 is positioned as a central organizer within MKS-related TZ assemblies: loss of TMEM67 or its ADAMTS9- mediated cleavage causes reduced recruitment of multiple MKS/B9 module proteins (TCTN1/2/3, TMEM237, CC2D2A, B9D2) to mature basal bodies/TZ, and disruption of the TZ necklace ultrastructure (DOI:10.1101/2024.09.04.611229).

TMEM43 functions as a tetraspanin-like membrane organizer at the inner nuclear membrane, maintaining nuclear envelope structure by organizing protein complexes including emerin, lamins, and SUN2. This is the primary biological function.
TMEM43 binds lamins (A-type and B-type) which is required for its retention at the inner nuclear membrane.

Structural light-chain subunit of cytoplasmic dynein-2: as a heterodimer with DYNLT1/DYNLT3 it binds the WDR60 intermediate chain in the dynein-2 tail and is required for stable motor function in retrograde intraflagellar transport.
Heterodimerization with the Tctex light chain DYNLT1 (dynein light chain binding), forming the light-chain pair that docks onto the dynein-2 intermediate chains.

Structural subunit of the calmodulin- and spoke-associated complex at the base of radial spoke 3 on axonemal doublet microtubules; provides the basal scaffold on which RS3 assembles and, through the CSC, connects the radial spokes to dynein regulatory machinery, supporting normal beating of motile cilia and sperm flagella. Only flagellated sperm motility is listed as the motility process: it is_a cilium movement involved in cell motility, which is_a cilium movement, so the accepted cilium movement annotation (supported by Tetrahymena waveform defects and mouse tracheal inner dynein arm loss, with human airway disease not established) is entailed rather than listed separately.

Transfers N-acetylglucosamine from UDP-GlcNAc to serine or threonine residues within folded EGF-like domains of secretory-pathway proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum lumen, initiating protein O-linked glycosylation. Human catalytic activity is established for the canonical 527-residue protein; the two shorter natural products remain functionally uncharacterized.

Supports cytoplasmic preassembly of outer and inner axonemal dynein arms through an assembly-factor mechanism that includes DNAI2 association. Human reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation and loss-of-function arm defects support this integrated function. Human HSP90-fragment Y2H and native mouse Hsp70/Hsp90 associations connect DNAAF6 to chaperone-associated assembly, while recruitment of those chaperones into a defined maturation complex remains a mechanistic model. Trans-Golgi enrichment is demonstrated in human airway cells; the binding assays do not establish the location or complete composition of the active assembly complex.

Transfers GalNAc from UDP-GalNAc in a beta-1,3 linkage to the terminal GlcNAc of the alpha-dystroglycan O-mannosyl glycan. This enzyme-catalyzed extension forms the core M3 trisaccharide required for subsequent POMK-dependent mannose phosphorylation and downstream functional glycosylation.

Mitochondrial complex I assembly factor that acts at early stages of complex I biogenesis and is specifically required for production/integration of the mitochondrially encoded ND1 (MT-ND1) subunit into the assembly intermediate.
Soluble B9-domain subunit bridging MKS1 and B9D1 in the transition-zone MKS module, which anchors TMEM67 and forms the ciliary membrane diffusion barrier.

ISCA1 is a core component of the late-acting mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] cluster assembly machinery. The ISCA1/ISCA2 heterodimer receives [2Fe-2S] clusters from GLRX5 and catalyzes their reductive fusion into [4Fe-4S] clusters, requiring electrons from FDX2/FDXR and the additional factor IBA57. This function is essential for maturation of mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] proteins including aconitase, respiratory complex I subunits, and lipoic acid synthase.

2-methoxy-6-polyprenyl-1,4-benzoquinol C-methyltransferase: catalyzes the sole C-methylation of the coenzyme Q head group, transferring a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the C2 position of the polyprenylated benzoquinol ring and producing S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine.
Intracellular protein with unknown molecular function

Thioredoxin-like oxidoreductase activity of MAGT1 within the OST-B complex. Via its lumenal, redox-active CXXC (CVVC) motif, MAGT1 forms transient mixed disulfides with the free thiols of nascent glycoprotein substrates in its predominantly oxidized state, delaying disulfide-bond formation so that STT3B can glycosylate cysteine-proximal acceptor sequons.

As an accessory subunit of the STT3B-containing oligosaccharyltransferase complex (OST-B), MAGT1 contributes to dolichyl-diphosphooligosaccharide-protein glycotransferase activity, promoting N-linked glycosylation of a subset of acceptor sequons (near cysteines / bracketed by disulfides) that are skipped by the STT3A complex. This is its core biological role.
Cytosolic J-domain co-chaperone of the HSP70 family that binds the cognate Hsp70 chaperone Hsc70 (HSPA8) and stimulates HSP70 ATPase activity via its J-domain HPD motif.

Dedicated co-chaperone for the biopterin-dependent aromatic amino acid hydroxylases (PAH, TH, TPH1, TPH2), binding these clients and assisting their proper folding and stability; loss of function reduces PAH activity and causes hyperphenylalaninemia.
Rubicon inhibits PIK3C3/VPS34 lipid kinase activity in the UVRAG-containing PI3KC3-C2 context and thereby negatively regulates autophagosome maturation and endosome maturation.
The C-terminal Rubicon homology (RH) domain binds GTP-bound Rab7, recruiting Rubicon to late endosomes/lysosomes where it inhibits PI3KC3-C2 and endosome/autophagosome maturation.

Binds polymerized microtubules through a directly assayed human CEP290 domain (residues 1695–1966), contributing to the structural organization of the ciliary transition zone and its protein-localization barrier. The purified domain assay uses bovine microtubules; full-length cellular recruitment can depend on CEP162 and other partners. Together with separate lipid-binding activity this supports, but does not reconstitute, a native Y-link tether. The detailed MKS-module assembly hierarchy is supported in C. elegans rather than proven in full for human CEP290.

Binds lipid membranes through the directly assayed human N-terminal region (residues 1–580), providing membrane-association capacity for ciliary organization. Human-cell CEP290 also contributes to ciliary-vesicle maturation and Rab8a/BBSome recruitment. The purified mixed-liposome assay does not establish lipid selectivity, an essential isolated amphipathic helix, direct fusion catalysis or simultaneous full-length membrane–microtubule bridging.

As a core subunit of IFT-A (with IFT122 and IFT144), IFT140 contributes to the cargo-carrying activity of the IFT-A complex, which together with cytoplasmic dynein-2 returns IFT-B, BBSome and membrane cargo from the ciliary tip to the base.
With its cargo adaptor TULP3, IFT-A (including IFT140) mediates ciliary entry of membrane proteins, notably G protein-coupled receptors, into primary cilia.

RPGRIP1L is the upstream assembly hub of the ciliary transition zone. It localizes to the TZ distal to CEP290 and binds NPHP4 directly within the NPHP1-NPHP4-NPHP8 module. It is required for recruitment of both MKS- and NPHP-module proteins (and, in worms, CEP-290) to the TZ, and so for TZ gate formation and cilium-dependent signalling. In photoreceptors it partners RPGR at the connecting cilium. It has no characterized enzymatic activity.

Binds TTBK2 through its N-terminal WW-domain region and recruits it to mother-centriole distal appendages to initiate cilium assembly. Human domain-mutant and targeted-fusion rescue experiments establish the recruitment role. This is kinase binding and positioning, not CEP164 kinase or kinase-activator activity. A complementary C-terminal Rabin8-binding route contributes ciliary membrane organization and Rab8 accumulation; direct Rab8 contact and a specific CEP164-mediated ternary bridge remain unestablished. Recent human-cell ultrastructure refines an obligatory initial-docking model toward membrane expansion after small-vesicle docking. The Rabin8 evidence remains a distinct interaction route; it does not establish an additional GEF or defined ternary-adaptor activity for CEP164.
Scaffolds CPLANE complex assembly at basal bodies to recruit IFT-A machinery for cilium biogenesis
Bridges NPHP4-DAAM1 interaction to organize subapical actin network required for basal body docking
Binds phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate (PI(3)P) preferentially via its N-terminal region to tether CPLANE on PI(3)P-rich vesicles near the nascent ciliary vesicle/basal body during late ciliogenesis
KCTD16 directly binds to the GABAB2 subunit C-terminal tail through its BTB/T1 domain, forming a 1:5 stoichiometric complex that is essential for GABA-B receptor function and signaling modulation
KCTD16 forms homopentamers via its BTB/POZ domain, a structural prerequisite for GABA-B receptor complex assembly
KCTD16 modulates GABA-B receptor pharmacology and signaling kinetics, conferring sustained non-desensitizing responses unlike KCTD12
As a subunit of the IFT-A peripheral subcomplex, WDR35 contributes to the cargo-carrier activity of IFT-A, binding membrane cargoes and mediating their entry into the primary cilium.
WDR35 participates in IFT-A-mediated retrograde intraflagellar transport along the axoneme.
WDR35 is required for cilium assembly; cells lacking it fail to produce normal cilia.

Structural subunit of the MKS/Tectonic module at the ciliary transition zone. It is needed to localize the module's components there, and through that module it gates the protein composition of the ciliary membrane.

Structural contribution to early ciliogenesis at the mother centriole. It is needed to assemble subdistal appendages, anchor microtubules, dock ciliary vesicles and extend the axoneme; the dependence varies between tissues.

CEP152 forms an integral scaffold with CEP63 around the proximal centriole. Its spatially distinct PLK4- and CPAP-binding regions organize centriole-duplication machinery; self-assembly and human mutant-rescue experiments connect this architecture to procentriole initiation.

During mitosis, CEP152 participates in a CEP63–CEP57 regulatory complex that restrains pericentrin recruitment and recruits APC/C at centrosomes. APC/C-dependent ubiquitylation and reduced centrosomal CEP152 permit remodeling of this complex, regulating spindle microtubule nucleation and assembly.

Binds autophagic SNARE assemblies and LC3/GABARAP-family proteins at the endolysosomal compartment, coordinating productive autophagosome-lysosome fusion and cargo clearance. SNARE binding is the directly demonstrated specific molecular function; a broader adaptor role remains a mechanistic model because human complex recognition or stabilization has not been distinguished from bringing two partners together.

Supports vesicular delivery of internalized endocytic cargo from endosomes to the late-endosome/lysosome compartment, enabling delivery of CpG DNA to endosomal TLR9. The molecular activity responsible for this endocytic role has not been distinguished from its autophagic Rab7/SNARE mechanism, so no separate molecular function is assigned.

ASXL3 activates BAP1 through its DEUBAD region as a regulatory partner of nuclear PR-DUB. The purified human DEUBAD fragment stimulates BAP1-mediated removal of nucleosomal H2A-K119 ubiquitin; BAP1 supplies the hydrolytic activity. This activation is distinct from ASXL3-mediated partner recruitment.

ASXL3 bridges BRD4 and the BAP1 complex through separable interaction regions, supporting BRD4 occupancy at active enhancers in human small cell lung cancer cells. Its BRD4-binding motif contacts the BRD4 ET domain directly, while deletion of that motif retains BAP1 association. This recruitment function is distinct from DEUBAD-mediated BAP1 activation and does not establish direct DNA recognition.

Catalyzes the final step of the CDP-ethanolamine (Kennedy) pathway of phosphatidylethanolamine biosynthesis: transfer of phosphoethanolamine from CDP-ethanolamine to a 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol acceptor to form phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) plus CMP, requiring a divalent cation (Mg2+/Mn2+). Acts as a multi-pass integral protein of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane.

Also synthesizes ether-linked phosphatidylethanolamine (plasmanyl-/plasmenyl-PE, a plasmalogen precursor) by transferring phosphoethanolamine from CDP-ethanolamine to a 1-O-alkyl-2-acylglycerol acceptor at the ER membrane; this ether-linked PE pool supports myelination and neurodevelopment.
ER membrane component of the GPI-GnT complex that binds PIGQ and promotes the first step of GPI anchor biosynthesis.
Cholesterol- and phospholipid-binding ER protein needed for normal sterol distribution between the ER and plasma membrane.
Phospholipid- and phosphoinositide-binding ARV1 homology domain.

Formylates a portion of the mitochondrial methionyl-tRNA(Met) pool, using 10-formyltetrahydrofolate as the formyl donor, to generate the N-formylmethionyl-tRNA(Met) initiator used by the mitochondrial translation initiation machinery, in the mitochondrial matrix.

Catalytic alpha/beta subunits of the Golgi GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase complex that recognise soluble lysosomal acid hydrolases and transfer GlcNAc-1-phosphate from UDP-GlcNAc to their high-mannose N-glycans, the first step in forming the mannose 6-phosphate lysosomal targeting signal.

PAM16 is the matrix-facing regulatory J-like cochaperone/adaptor subunit of the PAM complex that forms a subcomplex with Pam18/Tim14, recruits and restrains Pam18 activity, and tunes mtHsp70-powered import of presequence-containing proteins into the mitochondrial matrix.

Glutamine-dependent NAD(+) synthetase activity - the ATP-dependent amidation of deamido-NAD+ (NaAD) to NAD+ using L-glutamine as the nitrogen donor (hydrolyzed to L-glutamate), catalyzing the final, committed step of NAD+ de novo biosynthesis in the cytosol. NADSYN1 acts as a homohexamer.

ISCU is the primary scaffold for de novo [2Fe-2S] cluster assembly in the mitochondrial matrix. Recent structural studies (PMID:34824239, PMID:38627381) demonstrate that ISCU homodimerizes via Tyr-35 and receives persulfide sulfur from NFS1 Cys381 to Cys138. FDX2 provides reducing equivalents to complete cluster assembly.
ISCU functions as a scaffold/chaperone for Fe-S cluster assembly and subsequent transfer to recipient proteins via the HSPA9-HSCB chaperone system (PMID:38627381, PMID:23940031).
ISCU binds Fe2+ as part of the cluster assembly process. Mossbauer spectroscopy demonstrates iron coordination during assembly (PMID:38627381).
Tyr-35-mediated homodimerization is essential for [2Fe-2S] cluster synthesis. Mutation of Tyr-35 abolishes cluster assembly (PMID:34824239).
ISCU functions as a molecular scaffold/adaptor in cytoplasmic Fe-S cluster biogenesis via isoform 2 (ISCU1), coordinating with cytosolic NFS1 for cluster assembly.

NDUFAF3 is an assembly factor required for biogenesis of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I. Acting at the mitochondrial inner membrane, it tightly associates with its partner factor NDUFAF4 and with the iron-sulfur core subunits NDUFS2 and NDUFS3 to nucleate and stabilize an early membrane-arm assembly intermediate. It associates transiently with assembly intermediates and is not a subunit of the mature holoenzyme; loss of function causes isolated complex I deficiency.

Phosphopantetheine adenylyltransferase (PPAT) activity: adenylylates (R)-4'-phosphopantetheine with ATP to form 3'-dephospho-CoA, the fourth step of de novo CoA biosynthesis (EC 2.7.7.3), acting predominantly in the cytosol.

Dephospho-CoA kinase (DPCK) activity: phosphorylates 3'-dephospho-CoA with ATP to form coenzyme A, the fifth and final step of de novo CoA biosynthesis (EC 2.7.1.24), acting predominantly in the cytosol.

Provides an integral scaffold for BBSome organization through multiple subunit contacts. Pairwise association and assembly experiments support contacts with BBS1, BBS2, BBS5 and TTC8/BBS8. BBS9 joins the BBS2-BBS7 assembly intermediate through BBS2; reducing BBS9 impairs incorporation of additional subunits into the complex. This organizing activity contributes to protein localization to cilia: human-cell depletion disrupts BBSome assembly and ciliary entry. The complex associates with the ciliary membrane, and BBS9 localization to cilia is reported in human hTERT-RPE1 cells. BBS9 also contributes to cilium assembly in the tested mouse IMCD3 and zebrafish contexts; the magnitude depends on cell and organism, without establishing universal human-cell necessity. The CEP290 study separately shows loss of its centriolar-satellite pool after BBS9 depletion while transition-zone localization remains. These roles do not imply autonomous recognition of every ciliary cargo.
Rate-limiting enzyme of the NAD+ salvage pathway, condensing nicotinamide with 5-phospho-alpha-D-ribose 1-diphosphate (PRPP) to form nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), the immediate NAD+ precursor.
Performs the rate-limiting step of NAD+ regeneration from nicotinamide, recycling the nicotinamide released by NAD+-consuming enzymes (sirtuins, PARPs, CD38) to sustain the cellular NAD+ pool.

PSENEN/PEN-2 is an essential non-catalytic gamma-secretase subunit that promotes presenilin endoproteolysis, stabilizes and traffics the assembled complex, and enables presenilin-dependent intramembrane cleavage of APP, Notch receptors, and related membrane substrates.
ATP-independent small heat shock protein (holdase) that binds aggregation-prone and stress-destabilized client proteins, preventing their aggregation.

Co-chaperone partner of BAG3 that, with HSPA8/Hsp70 and STUB1/CHIP, drives chaperone-assisted selective autophagy (CASA), promoting aggrephagy/macroautophagic clearance of damaged clients (e.g. filamin, polyglutamine proteins) for muscle proteostasis.
Positive regulator of aggrephagy / selective autophagy, routing aggregation-prone misfolded clients for autophagic degradation as part of the cellular response to proteotoxic stress.

CRBN is the substrate-recognition subunit of the CRL4(CRBN) cullin-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase, binding DDB1 through its N-terminal Lon-like domain and recruiting substrate proteins through its C-terminal CULT (thalidomide-binding) domain to direct their ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.

CRBN binds thalidomide-class drugs (thalidomide, lenalidomide, pomalidomide) and molecular-glue/PROTAC degraders in its CULT domain; drug binding acts as a molecular glue that reprograms CRBN substrate specificity to recruit neosubstrates (e.g. IKZF1, IKZF3, CK1alpha) for degradation. This neosubstrate recruitment is drug-induced rather than an endogenous function.
ATP-dependent export of polyamines, preferentially spermine, from late endolysosomal compartments into the cytosol, coupled to the P-type ATPase cycle.

ATP-independent intramembrane carrier for Man(5)GlcNAc(2)-PP-dolichol in the ER membrane. Purified human RFT1 reconstituted into liposomes moves M5GN2-PP-Dol across the bilayer without ATP and with selectivity for the Man5 over the Man3 intermediate, positioning the glycan head group for luminal elongation to the mature Glc3Man9GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol precursor. The activity is demonstrated; whether it is the essential physiological role of the protein is contested, so it is stated here at the level the reconstitution supports.

Essential requirement for progression of dolichol-linked oligosaccharide assembly past the cytosolically oriented M5-DLO intermediate. Loss of RFT1 in yeast, in patient fibroblasts and in mammalian cells stalls the pathway at Man(5)GlcNAc(2)-PP-dolichol and hypoglycosylates secretory proteins, a defect rescued by wild-type cDNA. This requirement is agreed by both the transporter and the chaperone camps and is the claim the mutant-phenotype evidence actually licenses. No molecular_function is asserted for this entry, because the mutant-phenotype evidence establishes the pathway requirement without identifying the activity that satisfies it; the transport claim is stated separately above, at the level the reconstitution supports.

Na+-independent riboflavin (vitamin B2) transmembrane transporter activity: SLC52A2/RFVT2 is a multi-pass plasma-membrane protein that imports free riboflavin into cells with submicromolar affinity (KM ~0.33 uM), selective over FMN/FAD. Through this activity it drives cellular riboflavin transport, supplying the precursor of the flavin cofactors FAD/FMN and maintaining systemic and brain riboflavin homeostasis; loss of this transport causes riboflavin transporter deficiency (BVVLS2).
Recognizes gene-regulatory DNA and represses RNA polymerase II transcription, including HTR1A expression, through nuclear cooperation with cell-dependent Brg1 and chromatin-regulatory partners.

Coordinates PDK1 and Akt in an EGF-responsive cytosolic signaling complex, bringing the kinase and its substrate together without supplying kinase activity. Its effect depends on the cellular stimulus and adaptor concentration.

Thioredoxin-like protein-disulfide oxidoreductase activity of the lumenal thioredoxin domain (redox-active Cys99-Cys102 CXXC motif) that, within the STT3B/OST-B complex, forms transient mixed disulfides with free thiols in glycoprotein substrates, delaying disulfide-bond formation so that STT3B can glycosylate cysteine-proximal/otherwise-inaccessible acceptor sites.

As an accessory subunit of OST-B, TUSC3 contributes to the complex-level dolichyl-diphosphooligosaccharide-protein glycotransferase activity that transfers the high-mannose oligosaccharide onto asparagine acceptor sites, enabling STT3B-dependent protein N-linked glycosylation at the ER membrane.
FMN-dependent oxidation of pyridoxine 5'-phosphate and pyridoxamine 5'-phosphate to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (active vitamin B6), the terminal, rate-limiting step of PLP biosynthesis/salvage.
Binds FMN as its redox prosthetic group (one FMN per subunit), required for the oxidase catalytic mechanism.

Pyrroline-5-carboxylate reductase catalyzing the terminal, NAD(P)H-dependent step of proline biosynthesis (reduction of (S)-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate to L-proline) in mitochondria, acting on the glutamate-derived P5C pool.

LRIF1 binds the chromoshadow domain of HP1 through its C-terminal LRVCL PxVxL-class motif; the experimentally tested VCL-to-DCE substitution disrupts this interaction. In human cells this activity has separable outputs: LRIF1/HBiX1 and SMCHD1 connect H3K9me3/HP1 and XIST-H3K27me3 domains to compact the inactive X, while mitotic LRIF1 recruits HP1alpha to centromeres and thereby supports inner-centromere Aurora B activity and accurate mitotic sister chromatid segregation. Mouse evidence supports LRIF1-HP1gamma-dependent SMCHD1 loading at H3K9me3 chromosome-arm sites but also reveals a parallel inactive-X route, so it does not establish a universal recruitment mechanism for human LRIF1.

Human LRIF1 was shown to bind the D4Z4 repeat. That binding observation was not resolved by isoform. Separately, a homozygous nonsense variant that removes the long isoform is associated with D4Z4 relaxation and inappropriate DUX4 expression, and long-isoform knockdown derepresses DUX4 and its targets. Later somatic perturbation indicates that LRIF1 and SMCHD1 provide an auxiliary layer of D4Z4 repression rather than establishing all underlying chromatin features. The route that recruits LRIF1 to D4Z4 remains unknown, so this core unit records bounded chromatin binding and repression evidence without assigning an HP1- or SMCHD1-dependent recruitment mechanism or isoform-specific binding.

LRIF1 is a nuclear receptor transcriptional corepressor. Human LRIF1 binds RARalpha in vivo and in vitro, also interacts with other nuclear receptors, and contains a distal C-terminal repression domain distinct from its receptor-binding region. At the nuclear matrix it inhibits ligand-dependent RARalpha transcription partly by recruiting histone deacetylases. This focused activity is distinct from LRIF1's HP1-dependent chromatin-organization function and does not imply that every screen-detected interactor or every nuclear receptor is a physiological target.
Rho guanine nucleotide exchange factor that activates RhoA downstream of integrin engagement, supporting focal adhesion formation and cell migration.
GEF-independent scaffold that binds phosphorylated FAK and promotes FAK localization and activation at early adhesions, supporting focal adhesion assembly.

IFT172 is a peripheral IFT-B2 subunit that travels with anterograde trains and is required for cilium assembly and maintenance; its precise molecular activity (proposed roles in tip turnaround and train-membrane association) is not established in human cells, so no molecular-function term is asserted.

Promotes cytoplasmic maturation of assembly-competent outer and inner axonemal dynein arms, contributing these components to motile-cilium assembly, with conserved enrichment in DynAPs. Human arm defects and ortholog complementation/complex assays support the assembly role. DNAAF3/PF22 is a candidate arginine methyltransferase, supported by structural comparisons and loss of dynein arginine methylation in an algal null mutant; the intrinsic catalytic activity and its causal relationship to maturation remain unresolved.

Scaffolding of the GLI regulatory complex at the tip of the primary cilium. KIF7 brings the GLI transcription factors, their inhibitor SUFU and accessory enzymes such as the prolyl hydroxylase P4HA2 together in one place, using its C-terminal GLI-binding region while remaining anchored to axonemal microtubule plus ends. It performs no chemistry on these partners and does not carry them into the cilium - other motors do that - but without KIF7 the GLI-SUFU complex disperses into ectopic tip-like compartments along the axoneme and P4HA2 never reaches the cilium at all. This single adaptor activity accounts for both regulatory signs: it keeps GLI2 from being activated without ligand and full-length GLI3 from being processed into its repressor, and it permits SUFU turnover and SUFU-GLI dissociation when the pathway turns on.

Microtubule plus-end binding that limits axonemal microtubule growth. Purified KIF7 tracks the plus ends of growing microtubules, reduces their growth rate in a dose-dependent way and increases catastrophe frequency, and it does so only at plus ends - minus-end dynamics are unaffected. The activity requires ATP hydrolysis and is abolished by AMP-PNP, yet it is not motility: KIF7 cannot convert hydrolysis into stepping, so it acts as a stationary plus-end regulator rather than a transporter. In the cilium this is what sets cilium length, keeps the axoneme acetylated, glutamylated and stable, and confines the tip to a single compartment, which is the structural precondition for the scaffolding function above.

Supports cytoplasmic preassembly and incorporation of the outer and inner dynein arms during motile-cilium assembly. Human genetic and component-localization evidence establishes both arm classes; ortholog fractionation and rescue experiments support cytoplasmic preassembly. Human DNAAF1 associates with IFT88 and RUVBL1/RUVBL2, linking the assembly factor to ciliary trafficking machinery. The proposed coupling of dynein assembly to IFT delivery remains mechanistic inference: the direct dynein-client interfaces and a reconstituted transfer reaction are unresolved.

SEPSECS catalyzes the terminal, PLP-dependent step of selenocysteine biosynthesis, converting O-phospho-L-seryl-tRNA(Sec) plus selenophosphate to L-selenocysteinyl-tRNA(Sec) (EC 2.9.1.2). Acting as a homotetramer in the cytosol, it binds tRNA(Sec) and, with pyridoxal 5'-phosphate as an obligatory cofactor covalently bound to Lys284, performs the Sep-to-Sec conversion on the tRNA, producing the charged Sec-tRNA(Sec) used for selenoprotein synthesis.

SEPSECS binds pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) as its catalytic cofactor, covalently attached through a Schiff base to the active-site Lys284; removal or reduction of PLP abolishes activity, establishing PLP binding as integral to the enzyme's function.

SEPSECS binds tRNA(Sec) as an essential part of its catalytic cycle: the homotetramer engages the acceptor-, TPsiC-, and variable arms of tRNA(Sec), and this tRNA binding orients the substrate and activates the catalytic active site.

Structural component of the C2a projection of the axonemal central apparatus in motile cilia and sperm flagella; forms a homodimer at the C2a base and is required, together with CFAP65, MYCBPAP and CCDC108, for C2a integrity and central-pair stability, and hence for the normal ciliary beat pattern. No molecular function term is asserted: unlike CFAP47 and CFAP43, CFAP70 has no resolved contact map (the mouse model is an AlphaFold-assisted dimer fitted into C2a density, and its C-terminus has not been placed), so GO:0005200 structural constituent of cytoskeleton is plausible but not yet distinguishable from an assembly-factor role on the available data.

Required for sperm flagellum biogenesis during spermiogenesis: as an axonemal component and by assisting cytoplasmic preassembly of the calmodulin- and radial spoke-associated complex and manchette localisation of axonemal proteins; loss causes MMAF and male infertility (SPGF41).

Aminoacylates mitochondrial tRNA(Thr) with threonine in an ATP-dependent two-step reaction (threonyl-adenylate formation, then transfer to tRNA), and uses post-transfer editing to clear serine mischarged onto tRNA(Thr), supplying Thr-tRNA(Thr) for synthesis of the mtDNA-encoded respiratory-chain subunits in the mitochondrial matrix.

Hydrolyses Ser mischarged onto mitochondrial tRNA(Thr), the post-transfer editing reaction that makes the aminoacylation above accurate. This is a second catalytic activity rather than an aspect of the first: the chemistry is deacylation of a finished aminoacyl-tRNA, the substrate is the erroneous product, and the purified enzyme's proofreading was assayed as an activity separable from Thr activation and aminoacylation. It is listed as core because mischarging would otherwise put serine into every mtDNA-encoded respiratory-chain subunit, and because the P282L disease allele loses proofreading alongside charging.

Non-catalytic auxiliary subunit of the NatA N-terminal acetyltransferase complex that binds and activates the catalytic subunit NAA10, conferring N-terminal substrate specificity and serving as the scaffold for the NatA-associated factors HYPK and NAA50.
Anchors the NatA complex to the ribosome near the polypeptide exit tunnel, enabling co-translational N-terminal acetylation of nascent chains.

CEP57 binds microtubules and supports spindle microtubule organization. Human C-terminal constructs directly co-sediment with microtubules; mouse domain assays and human engineered Cep57S reconstitution further demonstrate tubulin recruitment, bundling and assembly capabilities. Cellular depletion/rescue connects these capabilities to centrosomal and spindle organization without requiring that all in-vitro conditions reproduce a native full-length condensate.

CEP57 provides cytoskeletal anchoring for centrosomal partners. Its N-terminal region directly recognizes the PCNT PACT domain, and recruitment/binding-deficient mutant and chimera experiments connect this physical interaction to organized pericentriolar material and centriole engagement in mitosis. The model specifies a protein anchor, not a kinase or a demonstrated fixed-stoichiometry motor complex.

Triacylglycerol lipase acting on cytoplasmic lipid droplets: hydrolyzes the first ester bond of stored triacylglycerol to give diacylglycerol and a fatty acid, the rate-limiting step of intracellular lipolysis. Activity depends on the patatin-domain active-site serine and is stimulated by ABHD5/CGI-58. The same hydrolysis drives turnover and shrinkage of the droplets themselves in adipose and non-adipose cells, which is why both triglyceride catabolism and lipid droplet disassembly are listed here rather than split across two entries: catalytically inactive ATGL still targets droplets but cannot reduce them, so the disassembly is a consequence of this one activity in this one location.

Binds GTP as a constituent of the U5 snRNP protein core that participates in spliceosomal pre-mRNA splicing. Native human U5 nucleotide-binding and splicing experiments establish the biochemical interaction and process involvement, while human tri-snRNP structures place EFTUD2 alongside PRPF8 in the assembled machinery. This nucleotide-bound role does not require assuming a demonstrated human GTPase motor cycle. Its structural participation includes snRNP and tri-snRNP assembly within the spliceosomal pathway; the process summary encompasses these assembly steps without assigning EFTUD2 the catalytic work of other subunits.

Contacts U5 snRNA as part of the conserved Snu114 ribonucleoprotein interface in the spliceosome. Direct crosslinking to U5 RNA is established in yeast, and the experimentally grounded PAINT placement supports inheritance by human EFTUD2. Human RNA-capture experiments independently support RNA binding, without resolving the same nucleotide contact or proving the proposed translocase mechanism.

ALG13 isoform 2 supplies the catalytic subunit of the membrane-associated ALG13–ALG14 enzyme, transferring GlcNAc from UDP-GlcNAc to GlcNAc-PP-dolichol to form the beta-1,4-linked chitobiose precursor during protein N-glycosylation. ALG14-dependent complex formation enables this activity on the cytoplasmic face of the ER.
Sequence- and structure-specific recognition of the SECIS element (a kink-turn stem-loop) in the 3'-UTR of selenoprotein mRNAs via the L7Ae/L30-family RNA-binding domain.

Recoding of in-frame UGA codons as selenocysteine during translation of selenoprotein mRNAs. SBP2 bound to SECIS docks onto the 40S ribosomal subunit (contacting eS31/RPS27A and 18S rRNA) and recruits the EEFSEC-Sec-tRNA(Sec) ternary complex, enabling co-translational selenocysteine insertion rather than termination.

At the plasma membrane, LRP12 binds the cytoplasmic tail of α4 integrins and restrains their activation by interfering with talin engagement, thereby balancing nascent-adhesion turnover and cell migration.

Alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase that adds the fourth and fifth mannose residues from GDP-mannose onto Man3GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol, producing Man5GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol on the cytoplasmic face of the ER membrane, as part of dolichol-linked oligosaccharide assembly for protein N-linked glycosylation.

Through building the Man5GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol LLO intermediate, ALG11 contributes to protein N-linked glycosylation; its deficiency causes hypoglycosylation of serum glycoproteins (ALG11-CDG / CDG type Ip).
Unconventionally secreted extracellular-matrix protein that binds dying-cell surfaces and recruits properdin to promote complement-mediated opsonization.
Secreted matrix-associated protein that binds extracellular matrix components such as hemicentin-1 in the choroid.

Binds microtubules and self-associates to support assembly and axonemal attachment of outer and inner dynein arms. Direct human recombinant microtubule binding complements human-protein rescue of both arm classes and conserved axonemal localization. Native human respiratory material contains apparent dimers, while recombinant full-length protein and defined fragments form oligomers. Native polymer geometry and the precise dynein/docking interface remain unresolved; native human arm-loss evidence is strongest for outer arms.
Polyglutamine protein from the SCA8 antisense transcript; known only as a disease-associated, inclusion-forming product of expanded alleles.

Magnesium-dependent, pH-neutral sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase (type-C neutral sphingomyelinase, EC 3.1.4.12) that hydrolyses membrane sphingomyelin to ceramide and phosphocholine at the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi, and outer nuclear envelope, thereby driving sphingomyelin turnover and ceramide production.
Binds the catalytic Mg2+ cofactor required for its neutral sphingomyelinase activity.

Mitochondrial Complex I assembly factor. NDUFAF8 is a small soluble matrix protein that binds and stabilizes the early Complex I assembly factor NDUFAF5. Its demonstrated molecular action is a specific protein-protein interaction with NDUFAF5 (not a catalytic activity); this stabilization is required for NDUFAF5-dependent maturation of the Q module during early Complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) biogenesis. NDUFAF8 is not a subunit of the mature holoenzyme. Loss of NDUFAF8 leads to NDUFAF5 degradation, a stalled Q-module intermediate, and isolated Complex I deficiency.

CFAP221 is a calmodulin-binding component of the conserved ciliary central-apparatus system that supports normal beating. Calcium-dependent binding is directly established for mouse Pcdp1 and algal FAP221 fragments; human airway loss-of-function establishes a waveform and transport defect despite retained cilia. The specific biochemical link from calmodulin occupancy to dynein regulation remains unresolved, and no motor or catalytic activity is assigned.

COA5 is a mitochondrial intermembrane-space assembly factor for cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV), acting at an early step of assembly and within the copper/heme metallochaperone machinery that matures the MT-CO1 and MT-CO2 catalytic metal centers.
Transmembrane MKS-module component that organizes the MKS part of the ciliary transition zone, being required (interdependently with B9D1) for TZ localization of B9D1, TMEM67 and MKS1.
As part of the TZ diffusion barrier, controls ciliary membrane composition (ARL13B, ADCY3, PKD2, INPP5E), thereby supporting Sonic hedgehog signalling and, in some tissues, ciliogenesis.
Synthesizes CDP-ribitol in the cytosol, supplying the activated ribitol-phosphate donor used by FKTN/FKRP during elaboration of the functional O-mannosyl glycan on alpha-dystroglycan.

Non-catalytic Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase)-specific assembly chaperone in the mitochondrial inner membrane. As the human ortholog of yeast Pet100p, PET100 binds early nuclear-encoded COX subunits (exemplified by the conserved interaction with COX subunit VIIa, COX7A2) and promotes their incorporation into an early COX assembly intermediate, forming a ~300 kDa subcomplex with Complex IV subunits. PET100 is essential for Complex IV maturation and assembly; its loss causes isolated Complex IV deficiency. No molecular-function term is asserted because PET100 has no catalytic activity and only binding/scaffolding-type molecular functions (the GOA "protein folding chaperone" term over-interprets this assembly role).

PET117 acts as a non-catalytic assembly chaperone at an early step of cytochrome c oxidase (mitochondrial respiratory chain complex IV) biogenesis, cooperating with the related PET100 chaperone and stabilizing the COX1 translational activator TACO1 to support assembly of the mtDNA-encoded core subunits.
